papers.title: Cumulative sport-related concussions alter cortical responses to acute aerobic exercise in rugby players.
papers.abstract: Rugby athletes sustain frequent head impacts, and cumulative sports-related concussion (SRC) exposure may alter neurophysiological function beyond overt symptoms. Acute aerobic exercise can enhance cognitive performance and modulate cortical activity, yet how acute exercise influences brain-behavior responses in collision-sport athletes and whether cumulative SRC exposure modifies these responses remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of acute aerobic exercise on neurocognitive and neurophysiological responses, and to determine whether these responses are modulated by sports-related concussion exposure in young male rugby athletes. Nineteen male rugby athletes completed resting EEG recordings (eye-opened [EO] and eye-closed [EC]; 3 min each) and cognitive testing (Stroop, King-Devick) before and after cycling at ~75% age-predicted maximal heart rate (HR). Athletes were categorized as no history of SRC (N.=8) or multiple SRC (N.=11). Exercise-related changes in cognition and relative EEG power were analyzed using repeated-measures and mixed-model Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), with associations examined using Spearman's and partial correlations. Stroop scores increased, and King-Devick test completion time decreased following exercise (both P<0.001). Temporal beta and gamma power showed significant time effects (EC beta P=0.026; EC gamma P<0.001; EO gamma P=0.003; EO beta P=0.050). Occipital gamma power during EO demonstrated a significant time × group interaction (P=0.012). SRC burden was negatively associated with EO occipital gamma power change (r=-0.482, P=0.037), while EO temporal gamma change was associated with King-Devick test change after controlling for SRC exposure (r=0.494, P=0.037). Acute aerobic exercise was associated with improved cognition and modulation of resting-state EEG activity, while cumulative SRC exposure impaired exercise-induced cortical responsivity, particularly in EO occipital gamma responses.
papers.journal: The Journal of sports medicine and physical fitness

papers.title: Isoproterenol for Bradycardia Associated Prolonged QT Interval After Mixed Drug Overdose.
papers.abstract: Prolonged QT interval is a marker for risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Risk factors include medications, bradycardia, female sex, genetics, advanced age, structural abnormalities, and electrolyte derangements. This case describes an 18-year-old woman with an extensive psychiatric history who overdosed on escitalopram and guanfacine in a suicide attempt. At 33 hours from ingestion, QTc interval measured 658 milliseconds with persistent bradycardia. Isoproterenol successfully prevented emergence of torsades de pointes (TdP). Coingestion of substances in the setting of overdose requires prompt identification of toxidromes in anticipation of potential complications. Management for prolonged QTc interval should be based on TdP risk assessment considering patient and clinical factors. In select hospitalized patients with sinus bradycardia at high risk for TdP, early use of isoproterenol may be used to prevent the occurrence of adverse cardiac events.

papers.title: Impact of Schizophrenia on Outcomes Following Non-Invasive Ventilation for Acute Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure in COPD.
papers.abstract: Limited data describe outcomes in people with comorbid schizophrenia when admitted with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure (AHRF). This study compared outcomes in people with COPD requiring non-invasive ventilation (NIV), with and without schizophrenia, to identify priorities for intervention and research. This is a retrospective cohort study from a single Australian quaternary referral hospital of people with COPD requiring NIV for AHRF over 5 years from 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2024, excluding admissions between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted usual practices. Primary outcomes were length of stay (LOS) and NIV duration (days). Secondary outcomes included NIV discontinuation reason, challenges to NIV and readmission. Descriptive and comparative statistics summarised variables by schizophrenia status and assessed between-group differences. Cox proportional hazards models assessed survival, while association between schizophrenia and readmission was analysed using competing-risks regression. Prevalence of schizophrenia is higher in this cohort than general population, comprising 36 (19%) of 186 individuals, and 97 (30%) of 328 admissions. Those with schizophrenia were younger (66.6 vs. 72.5 years, p = 0.001), with more current smokers (75% vs. 42.7%, p = 0.005) and had admissions with shorter LOS (6 vs. 9 days, p = 0.043) and NIV duration (3 vs. 5 days, p = 0.021). There was no significant difference in reason for NIV discontinuation between the groups. Readmission rates were higher in the schizophrenia group (44.4% vs. 24.0%, p = 0.025). Age at death was lower for those with schizophrenia (67.3 vs. 77.4 years, p < 0.001). People with schizophrenia had shorter LOS and NIV use, higher readmission rates, higher prevalence of current smokers and younger age at presentation and death. These findings suggest that schizophrenia is an at-risk subgroup in AHRF, highlighting the need for collaborative action.

papers.title: Healthy Sleep Mitigates the Association Between Cardiometabolic Disease and Poorer Cognitive and Brain Health.
papers.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), including type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, are important risk factors for dementia. We examined whether healthy sleep can support cognitive and brain health in people with CMDs. The study included data from 408 977 adults from the UK Biobank. CMDs were defined using medical records, medication use, and medical history. Sleep patterns were defined using a composite score incorporating sleep duration, chronotype, insomnia symptoms, snoring, and daytime sleepiness. A subsample (n=34 913) underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging; volumes of total brain, gray matter, white matter, hippocampus, and white matter hyperintensities were ascertained. Associations of joint CMD (yes/no) and sleep (healthy, intermediate, poor) status with global and domain-specific cognitive scores and brain magnetic resonance imaging measures were examined using linear regression models. At baseline, 54017 (13.2%) participants had at least one CMD. In joint exposure analysis, performance in global cognition (β=0.02 [95% CI, 0.01-0.05]), verbal/numeric reasoning (β=0.07 [95% CI, 0.01-0.12]), and processing speed (β=0.07 [95% CI, 0.04-0.10]) was significantly higher among individuals with CMDs and a healthy sleep pattern, compared with those with CMDs and a poor sleep pattern. Similarly, in neuroimaging analyses, participants with CMDs and a healthy versus poor sleep pattern showed significantly larger total brain volume (β=0.22 [95% CI, 0.08-0.35]), gray matter volume (β=0.23 [95% CI, 0.09-0.36]), and white matter volume (β=0.19 [95% CI, 0.05-0.33]). Healthy sleep may attenuate the associations of CMDs with poorer cognitive performance and markers of brain atrophy. The findings highlight sleep as a modifiable factor that may support cognitive and brain health in individuals with CMDs.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

papers.title: Pterostilbene and 3'-Hydroxypterostilbene Alleviate AOM/DSS-Induced and Chronic Jet Lag-Exacerbated Colon Cancer.
papers.abstract: Chronic circadian disruption is associated with colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether it exacerbates CRC progression and influences the protective effects of dietary interventions remains unclear. We examined pterostilbene (PSB) and 3'-hydroxypterostilbene (3'-HPSB) in an azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium-induced CRC mouse model exposed to chronic jet lag. Chronic jet lag aggravated disease activity, intestinal pathology, inflammation, and tumor burden. Dietary PSB and 3'-HPSB supplementations, initiated before CRC induction, attenuated these pathological changes and reduced macroscopic tumors (≥2 mm) by approximately 36% and 49%, respectively. These effects were accompanied by alterations in circadian clock-related and Wnt/β-catenin signaling-related proteins and by reduced intestinal epithelial proliferation. Supplementation was also associated with changes in gut microbiota composition and fecal short-chain fatty acid levels. These findings support preventive/protective effects of PSB and 3'-HPSB under chronic circadian disruption and identify associated molecular and microbial alterations warranting further mechanistic investigation.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

papers.title: Harnessing Neuroendocrine and Circadian Clocks in Beneficial Insects for Agricultural Chrono-Management.
papers.abstract: Pollinators and natural enemies provide essential agricultural ecosystem services that are regulated by circadian clocks, hormones, and biogenic amines. This review synthesizes research on the integration between neuroendocrine systems and circadian clocks across different taxa, identifying both conserved regulatory mechanisms and lineage-specific adaptive traits. These multilayered interactions coordinate insect behavior, life-history development, and the alignment of insect activities with available resources. We propose agricultural chrono-management, a framework to improve ecosystem services by using targeted environmental cues to align beneficial insect activity with farming schedules. However, most evidence so far comes from the laboratory and controlled studies, and field validation remains limited. We further evaluated the feasibility, ecological risks, and climate resilience of photoperiodic regulation, nutritional modulation, and synthetic ecological interventions. Key future research priorities include multiomics integration, large-scale field validation, and predictive modeling of ecosystem services. This synthesis links molecular-level regulatory mechanisms to ecological outcomes and establishes a foundational framework for climate-resilient management of beneficial insects.

papers.title: Poor Test-Retest Stability of Nocturnal REM Sleep Onset Markers in Narcolepsy Type 1.
papers.abstract: To assess the test-retest stability of nocturnal sleep-onset REM periods (nSOREMPs) in untreated patients with narcolepsy type 1 (NT1), and of nocturnal direct REM (nDREM) transitions and their clinical and biological correlates. We included consecutive children and adults with NT1 diagnosed according to ICSD-3-TR criteria based on excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, multiple sleep latency test (MSLT) findings, or CSF hypocretin-1 deficiency, without using nSOREMPs for diagnosis. All patients underwent two untreated overnight polysomnographic (PSG). nSOREMP was defined as REM sleep within 15 minutes of sleep onset, and nDREM as direct transition from wakefulness or N1 to REM sleep without intervening N2 or N3 sleep. Among 227 patients (108 males; mean age 31.6 years (SD=14.8)), nSOREMPs were present on both PSGs in 41.8%, on one only in 35.7%, and absent on both in 22.4%, yielding poor test-retest agreement (κ=0.26, 95% CI 0.14-0.39, McNemar test p=0.10). Persistent nSOREMPs were associated with younger age, shorter sleep latency, more SOREMPs on the MSLT, and lower hypocretin levels, but not with PSG interval, symptom severity, or medication history. nDREM was present on both PSGs in 15.9%, on one PSG in 37.4%, and absent on both in 46.7%, with poor stability and persistence associated with younger age, shorter MSLT sleep latency, and lower CSF hypocretin levels. nSOREMPs and nDREMs showed limited test-retest stability in untreated children and adults with NT1. Their association with age, MSLT findings, and hypocretin levels suggest variable REM dysregulation rather than stable individual traits. Absence of nSOREMP even on two PSG should not exclude NT1.

papers.title: Cardiac Autonomic Association Atlas of Sleep Parameters in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Large-Scale Cohort-Based Observational Study.
papers.abstract: To systematically evaluate associations between multidimensional sleep parameters and non-invasive cardiac autonomic nervous system metrics derived from heart rate variability (HRV) in patients with obstructive sleep apnea, and to identify the autonomic pathways most closely linked to sleep disturbances. Using overnight polysomnography from the Shanghai Sleep Health Study cohort, a three-stage dimensionality-reduction strategy compressed 147 sleep parameters and 68 HRV metrics into 59 parameters (5 functional domains) and 25 metrics (5 autonomic domains). For each sleep-HRV pair, multivariable linear regression was adjusted for age, sex, BMI, blood pressure, fasting glucose, and lipids. False discovery rate was controlled via the Benjamini-Yekutieli method, with robustness assessed through 2,000 bootstrap resamples and an independent test set. Among 9,359 subjects (training 6,551; test 2,808), 646 of 1,475 associations were significant after correction; 602 (93.2%) showed directional consistency across bootstraps, with 80.3% test-set reproducibility. The Regulatory Complexity and Sympathovagal Balance domains were enriched in Nocturnal Hypoxemia (71.7%, 63.3%) and Fragmentation & Arousal (66.7%, 58.3%), whereas Baroreflex & Ectopic Domain was systematically sparse (6.7% to 20.0%). Core associations arose almost exclusively from Respiratory Event Burden and Nocturnal Hypoxemia, diverging directionally: positive with Lempel-Ziv complexity, skewness, and VLF power, yet negative with Higuchi fractal dimension, normalized corrected conditional entropy. Nocturnal Hypoxemia and Fragmentation & Arousal are preferentially linked to nonlinear dynamics reflecting Regulatory Complexity and Sympathovagal Balance, whereas Baroreflex & Ectopic metrics are only selectively engaged. This atlas provides a unified framework for generating testable hypotheses and selecting clinically meaningful autonomic biomarkers.

papers.title: Clinical Trajectory of Late-Onset Delusional Disorder Toward Evolving Dementia With Lewy Bodies.
papers.abstract: Recent clinical observations indicate that late-onset psychosis can precede the onset of dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). However, its longitudinal clinical trajectory remains poorly understood. Delusional disorder (DD) in older adults is relatively uncommon and poor insight frequently leads to refusal of psychiatric care, limiting available data despite its long-standing diagnostic recognition. This article focuses on late-onset DD in relation to subsequent development of DLB. We revisited our previously reported cases in which delusions were the initial manifestation of Lewy body disease (LBD) and aimed to identify the shared clinical features to help delineate more homogeneous subgroups within the heterogeneous spectrum of late-onset psychosis. These cases with late-onset DD revealed a recurring phenotype characterised by onset in the 50s and 60s, reluctance to seek psychiatric care, eventual hospitalisation, poor antipsychotic tolerance and delayed emergence of dementia accompanied by core features of DLB. Clinicopathological examination of four cases raises the hypothesis that persistent delusions may emerge in the presence of relatively restricted Lewy pathology, preceding the development of widespread cortical involvement and overt dementia. Relative preservation of neuronal populations in the substantia nigra may account for the absence of parkinsonism during the early phases dominated by isolated delusions. Despite long-standing delusions beginning in the 50s and 60s, a common age range for DLB onset (mid-70s and older) was observed, indicating an exceptionally prolonged prodromal period. These findings suggest that late-onset DD associated with LBD may follow a clinical trajectory distinct from that of mild cognitive impairment with Lewy bodies (MCI-LB), the most common clinical phenotype of prodromal DLB. Differentiating DD from broader late-onset psychosis categories may facilitate future research by reducing heterogeneity and stratifying cases with potentially prolonged periods without dementia or parkinsonism. Clinical and pathological reports of late-onset DD remain scarce and further case documentation is warranted.
papers.journal: Psychogeriatrics : the official journal of the Japanese Psychogeriatric Society

papers.title: Feasibility of Heart Rate-Based Total Daily Energy Expenditure Estimation of Pararescuemen in Garrison.
papers.abstract: Hammond, KG, Bair, AC, Strang, AJ, Young, JC, Kruskall, LJ, Dunnick, DD, and Schilling, BK. Feasibility of heart rate-based total daily energy expenditure estimation of pararescuemen in garrison. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Pararescuemen are a group of Air Force Special Operations Forces who engage in vigorous daily training to prepare for deployment operations. This training can elicit high-energy expenditure, yet few studies have measured the energy expenditure of these airmen while at their home station (in garrison). Twelve operational pararescuemen (age: 27 ± 3 years; years of service: 5 ± 3 years) were assessed for resting energy expenditure, heart rate (HR) at rest and during initial exercise, and the HR-oxygen consumption (V̇o2) linear equation. Subjects' HR was recorded over 2 normal training days and used to estimate total daily energy expenditure (TDEE). Subjects reported an average 9 ± 2 hours of sleep per night of analysis and had an average basal metabolic rate = 82 ± 4 kcal·h-1. Average TDEE was 4,021 ± 890 kcals. Pararescuemen expend high levels of energy during routine training at their home station, similar to those of other elite military groups. Observed and reported high-energy expenditures in pararescuemen suggest further investigation into energy intake in this population to optimize performance.
papers.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research

papers.title: Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan Attenuates Neuronal Injury in LPS-Treated HT22 Cells and PCPA-Induced Insomnia-Model Rats.
papers.abstract: Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan (TWBXD) is traditionally used for sleep disorders, but its neuroprotective mechanisms remain unclear. This study evaluated a cinnabar-free modified TWBXD preparation in cellular and animal models, focusing on phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT) expression, autophagy-related markers, inflammation, and apoptosis. An aqueous TWBXD extract was profiled by untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Candidate compounds annotated by LC-MS and checked against PubChem records were used for target prediction, followed by intersection with insomnia-related genes, protein-protein interaction analysis, and functional enrichment. TWBXD-containing serum was evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-treated HT22 hippocampal neuronal cells. Rapamycin and 3-methyladenine were used to probe autophagy-related processes. In p-chlorophenylalanine (PCPA)-treated rats, pentobarbital-induced sleep responses, locomotor activity, anxiety-like behavior, spatial learning and memory, and hippocampal CA1 pathology were assessed. Twenty high-confidence candidate compounds yielded 553 predicted human targets, of which 144 overlapped with insomnia-related genes. Network analysis identified 10 candidate hub genes, including AKT1, MTOR, BCL2, TNF, and IL6, and highlighted PI3K-Akt, autophagy, apoptosis, and inflammatory pathways. In LPS-treated cells, rapamycin shifted several autophagy-related and inflammatory markers toward control levels. TWBXD-containing serum increased Beclin 1 expression and the microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3-II to light chain 3-I (LC3-II/LC3-I) ratio, decreased p62, interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), Bax, and caspase 3, and increased interleukin-10 (IL-10) and Bcl-2. PI3K and AKT protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) levels also shifted toward control levels. Several TWBXD-associated molecular changes were attenuated by 3-methyladenine. In PCPA-treated rats, TWBXD improved pentobarbital-induced sleep responses, anxiety-like behavior, and spatial learning and memory and alleviated hippocampal CA1 neuronal injury. These findings support the neuroprotective effects of cinnabar-free modified TWBXD in the models examined. Behavioral and histological improvements were accompanied by changes in PI3K/AKT expression and autophagy-, inflammation-, and apoptosis-related markers.

papers.title: Eat, sleep - How and when to treat: A guide for leveraging behavioral sleep medicine for co-occurring insomnia in eating disorder treatment.
papers.abstract: Insomnia symptoms are highly prevalent among individuals with eating disorders, and evidence suggests a bidirectional relationship between sleep disturbances and disordered eating. Although effective and flexible psychological and behavioral treatments for insomnia are available, there is limited research and a lack of clinical guidelines on addressing insomnia in the context of eating disorder concerns. This paper outlines the potential benefits of prioritizing treatment of comorbid insomnia and discusses clinical frameworks for addressing these co-occurring conditions. We highlight how targeting insomnia may improve overall functioning and support eating disorder recovery. A clinical case example is included in the supplement to illustrate decision-making processes that may assist clinicians in determining optimal treatment sequencing and integration for patients presenting with both insomnia and disordered eating symptoms.

papers.title: Tick tock: how the body's circadian clock keeps cardiometabolic rhythm in check.
papers.abstract: The circadian clock orchestrates the internal timing of numerous physiological processes through an approximately 24-h cycle. It comprises a hypothalamic central clock, which responds to light cues and entrains peripheral clocks within individual cells and organs that, depending on the tissue, regulate gene expression across diverse biological functions in a tissue-specific manner. Peripheral clocks are also entrained by feeding and exercise-related cues, enabling their synchronization with feeding rhythm and physiology. Together, these clocks maintain a complex molecular network essential for metabolic homeostasis. Disruption of circadian rhythms, driven by genetic, environmental, or behavioral factors, is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to cardiometabolic disorders. Modern lifestyles, including shift work, irregular sleep, prolonged exposure to artificial light at night, jet lag, and erratic eating schedules, misalign circadian clocks with environmental cues, contributing to disruption of circadian rhythms or chronodisruption. This misalignment alters hormonal regulation, promotes systemic inflammation, and impairs metabolic balance, thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease, obesity, type 2 diabetes, and related complications. The present review examines the mechanistic roles of core circadian clock genes in cardiometabolic health, highlighting their regulation of physiological processes in peripheral organs such as the heart, liver, and adipose tissue. We further discuss how circadian clock disruption accelerates disease onset and progression and explore emerging therapeutic strategies, including pharmacological modulation of the molecular circadian clock components and personalized chronotherapy. These approaches offer promising avenues to restore circadian alignment and mitigate cardiometabolic risk.

papers.title: Effects of Creative Arts Therapy on Psychological Outcomes and Stress-Related Physiological Markers in Children With Cancer: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Children with cancer frequently experience psychological distress and symptom-related challenges during diagnosis, treatment, and hospitalization. Creative arts therapy (CAT) has been used as a complementary approach to support emotional expression, coping, and stress regulation; however, its effects on psychological outcomes and stress-related physiological markers remain unclear. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). The CINAHL, Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Sciences databases were searched for quantitative studies published between 2014 and 2025. Eligible studies included children and adolescents with cancer who received CAT. A total of 4860 records were identified, of which 26 studies met the inclusion criteria and were synthesized narratively. CAT was generally associated with reductions in anxiety, depression, stress, distress, fear, procedural pain, and emotional discomfort, and with improvements in coping, emotional regulation, sleep quality, relaxation, happiness, and quality of life. A smaller subset of studies reported potential benefits for physiological markers, including heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, cortisol levels, hemodynamic status, and hematologic indicators. CAT may support psychological well-being, symptom relief, and stress regulation among children with cancer and may be a useful complement to supportive care in pediatric oncology, although further rigorous trials using standardized outcomes are needed.

papers.title: Host Physiology and Environmental Stress as Potential Modifiers of Mycoplasma synoviae Disease Severity in Chickens.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma synoviae (MS) is a poultry pathogen associated with respiratory disease, infectious synovitis, eggshell abnormalities, and reduced production performance. Clinical expression varies substantially among farms, flocks, and individual birds, ranging from subclinical infection to respiratory, articular, reproductive, or systemic disease. This variation suggests that pathogen presence alone may not fully explain differences in disease severity. This narrative review synthesizes evidence relevant to the hypothesis that MS disease severity may reflect interactions between pathogen colonization and host physiological state. Experimental and field studies demonstrate that MS infection involves respiratory colonization, lateral transmission, strain-dependent differences in infectivity and virulence, adhesion to host ligands, and tissue tropism. Studies specifically investigating MS infection also document inflammatory, oxidative, apoptotic, and metabolic responses in infected chickens. The review then evaluates host physiological pathways and environmental stress responses that may modify these outcomes, including corticosterone signaling, the growth hormone-insulin-like growth factor 1 (GH-IGF-1) axis, melatonin and circadian regulation, and cytokine networks. These systems are known to influence immune competence, redox balance, epithelial integrity, tissue repair, and metabolic allocation in chickens. The available evidence supports a mechanistic framework in which pathogen factors and host physiology may interact to modify MS disease expression. Evaluation of the available evidence indicates that MS-specific support is strongest for pathogen factors and tissue responses; however, none of the proposed environmental, endocrine, or circadian modifiers has been causally tested in an MS challenge model, and genetic, microbiota, and omics-based biomarker evidence remains preliminary. This framework therefore provides testable hypotheses and candidate measurements for future studies.

papers.title: A Lightweight EEG-Based Alzheimer's Disease Detection Framework on an Edge-Computing Platform Toward Future Intelligent Digital Twin Systems.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) progresses slowly through several stages until the patient reaches full cognitive decline. The electroencephalography (EEG) alterations associated with AD often emerge before symptom onset, suggesting that accessible and repeated EEG-based assessment could facilitate earlier detection and longitudinal monitoring. However, this type of assessment requires an AD detection model operating on edge-computing platforms within the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT). At present, many existing AD detection models rely on complex deep learning architectures with numerous parameters, which significantly limit their practicality for on-edge deployment. We propose an on-edge AD detection framework comprising a lightweight dilated hybrid deep learning (DHDL) model with a channel selection approach to reduce the computational and power demands on the evaluated edge-computing platform. A key architectural component is the inclusion of dual-granularity dilated temporal convolutions. This method expands the receptive field at two scales to capture both short- and long-term temporal features from EEG signals without increasing the number of parameters. Subsequently, several hybrid lightweight layers extract distinct temporal and spatial features and are integrated with attention mechanisms. Additionally, our channel selection approach first forms an initial subset of EEG channels guided by individual channel classification accuracy, and then iteratively refines the selected channels using hill-climbing optimization. Here, we evaluated our framework on two publicly available EEG datasets recorded for the same group of subjects (n = 48 subjects): a conventional closed-eye (CE) dataset and a more challenging open-eye (OE) dataset. Validation followed a subject-independent Leave-2-Subjects-Out (L2SO) cross-validation protocol. Real-time deployment was tested on an edge-computing platform. The proposed framework achieved 92.56% accuracy for the CE dataset and 75.15% accuracy for the OE dataset. Inference required 10.45 ms and 8.23 ms per segment for the CE and OE datasets, respectively, and consumed 9.69 mJ and 6.95 mJ of energy per segment, respectively. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework as a real-time, on-edge inference module for AD detection. Although a complete intelligent digital twin system is not implemented in this work, the proposed framework can serve as an inference component for future digital twin systems, supporting early AD detection and progression monitoring.

papers.title: Dynamics of Sleep Architecture and Nocturnal Oxygen Saturation During Acclimatization at Intermediate Altitude: A Longitudinal Observational Study in Elite Athletes.
papers.abstract: Athletes typically undergo training camps living and sleeping at intermediate altitudes (1500-2500 m). Hypoxia reshapes sleep through central circuits regulating arousal, chemoreflex gain and sympathetic outflow. However, the relationship between peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) and sleep architecture and how it co-evolves during acclimatization, is unclear. We tested whether SpO2 differs across sleep stages at intermediate altitude and whether its recovery is stage specific. Seventeen mogul-ski athletes (seven women) travelled from Montréal (Canada) to Tignes (France) for a 2-week altitude training camp (AltitudeCamp; 2100 m) in June 2025. During the first week (6 nights) and the last night of AltitudeCamp, athletes were provided with a validated ring pulse oximeter and an electroencephalography (EEG) headband. We evaluated the changes in sleep stage distribution across successive nights, scored on 30-second epochs and synchronized with oximetry data. Model estimates are reported as mean ± Standard Error (SE), raw data as mean ± Standard Deviation (SD). Average total sleep time was 429 ± 47 min (mean ± SD) and did not change during AltitudeCamp (p = 0.939). Across the first week, %N3 decreased logarithmically (β = -2.35 ± 0.72%/ln (night), p = 0.002) and %Rapid eye movement sleep (REM) increased logarithmically (β = 3.13 ± 0.88%/ln (night), p < 0.001), with no changes in %Wake, %N1, or %N2. SpO2 was lower during AltitudeCamp (95.2 ± 0.3%) than measures obtained in normoxia (98 ± 0.4%; p < 0.001), and overnight heart rate (HR) was 7 ± 2 beats per minute (bpm) higher than the habitual 58 ± 3 bpm observed in normoxia (p = 0.005). Wake SpO2 increased by 0.13 ± 0.01 percentage points per night (p < 0.001), with faster recovery in N1 (0.19 ± 0.02 percentage points/night; p = 0.006) and REM (0.23 ± 0.01 percentage points/night; p < 0.001), while N2 and N3 did not differ from Wake. HR declined by 0.79 bpm/night during Wake, similar to N3 (p = 0.26), but larger than the decline in N1 (p = 0.024) and REM (p < 0.001). In N2, HR did not evolve during the first week at altitude. At intermediate altitude, nocturnal SpO2 and HR show sleep-stage-specific dynamics that mirror central ventilatory and autonomic adaptation to hypoxia. Our data suggest that acclimatization is not uniform across sleep stages, and that the first 2 nights after ascent may capture the most rapid adjustments despite similar total sleep duration. Sleep therefore offers a heterogeneous and ecologically valid index of central nervous system (CNS) acclimatization, which can be monitored longitudinally with wearable EEG-oximetry.

papers.title: Neural Mechanisms of Smartphone Addiction: A Systematic Review of Neuroimaging and Related Neurophysiological/Neurostimulation Studies.
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of smartphones into daily life has undeniably brought immense convenience, but it has also introduced challenges, particularly in the form of problematic smartphone use (often referred to as smartphone addiction). This form of behavioral dependence has been linked to significant impairments in physiological, psychological, and social domains. In this systematic review, we investigated the neural underpinnings of smartphone addiction through various brain imaging techniques, with a particular emphasis on studies employing functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electroencephalography (EEG), functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and complementary neurostimulation as well as neurophysiological methods. Relevant data were retrieved from major academic databases-including CNKI, PubMed, and Web of Science-using a thorough keyword-based search strategy. A total of 41 studies were analyzed and categorized according to their research methods, participant characteristics, targeted populations, and key findings. We identified a consistent association between smartphone addiction and alterations in brain structure and activity, as well as its co-occurrence with a range of mental health challenges. These findings collectively underscore the pressing need for further research into the neurobiological mechanisms of smartphone addiction and the development of targeted interventions to mitigate its adverse effects. The PROSPERO Registration: CRD420261369691, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261369691.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Graph Analysis Reveals Enhanced Alpha-Band Integration in High-IQ Individuals: The MENSA-Connect Project.
papers.abstract: To assess whether resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) connectivity differs between high-intelligence individuals (MENSA members) and controls using graph-theory metrics: clustering coefficient, characteristic path length, and small-worldness. Resting-state 64-channel EEG data were recorded in 29 MENSA participants and 20 controls. Functional connectivity was estimated using Lagged Linear Coherence across delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands. Graph-theory measures were computed using sLORETA and the Brain Connectivity Toolbox. Between-group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test; p-values were corrected for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure, and effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. Compared with controls, MENSA participants showed significantly lower characteristic path length in the alpha band (Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) critical value = 0.004), indicating greater global network integration. In the beta band, they showed a higher clustering coefficient (BH critical value = 0.008), reflecting greater local specialization; together with a higher characteristic path length (BH critical value = 0.013), suggesting reduced global communication. No significant group differences were observed in small-worldness across frequency bands. High-Intelligence Quotient (IQ) individuals show a frequency-dependent resting-state cortical organization, characterized by enhanced alpha-band integration and increased beta-band local specialization. These findings support a nuanced neural-efficiency model of intelligence without changes in small-world architecture. Given the cross-sectional and observational design, these findings should be regarded as associative rather than causal and require replication in larger, independent samples. These findings indicate frequency-specific differences in functional network organization, although their cognitive implications remain to be established.

papers.title: The Role of Drosophila Toll Receptors in the Central Nervous System.
papers.abstract: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are evolutionarily conserved pattern recognition receptors that play pivotal roles in innate immunity by detecting pathogen-associated molecular patterns. While initially characterized for their function in dorsoventral patterning and antifungal defense in Drosophila, the Toll family is now understood to have undergone a functional expansion in the nervous system. This review synthesizes the current understanding of the nine Drosophila Toll receptors (Toll-1 to Toll-9) and their roles in the central nervous system (CNS). We discuss how these receptors, particularly through non-canonical signaling pathways, function as neurotrophin receptors and cell surface recognition molecules. They mediate a wide range of cellular processes, from axon guidance to synaptic partner matching and the regulation of neuronal survival versus apoptosis through the competitive recruitment of adaptor proteins such as dMyD88 and Sarm. We further explore the involvement of Toll signaling in adult brain structural plasticity, sleep homeostasis, and behavioral responses to environmental stressors such as ethanol. Importantly, this article addresses the context-dependent duality of Toll signaling in neuropathology, dysregulation, and aberrant activation, which are closely related to neurodegeneration, lifespan determination, and infection responses. Through this timely summary of current research, this review highlights the molecular switches that govern Toll receptor functional states and their roles in neuro-immune interactions, with implications for understanding neurological diseases in vertebrates.

papers.title: Multiscale Neurodynamic Alterations in Major Depressive Disorder Revealed by Lempel-Ziv Complexity of Multi-Paradigm Resting-State EEG.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) abnormalities in major depressive disorder (MDD) have predominantly been examined through single-frequency band analyses or single-scale nonlinear measures, and largely within a single resting-state paradigm, which limits the characterization of regulatory interactions across temporal scales. In this study, we investigated dynamic transitions and integrative patterns of multiscale EEG activity in MDD across multiple resting-state paradigms, with a focus on characterizing alterations in multiscale neural dynamic organization. Based on multiscale Lempel-Ziv Complexity (LZC), we derived two classes of features quantifying the Scale-Dependent Variation Slope and the Cross-Scale Correlation Coefficient. Resting-state EEG from the MDD Patients and Healthy Controls EEG Data (MPHC) was analyzed under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions to compare multiscale regulatory dynamics between patients with MDD and healthy controls. Patients with MDD showed impaired complexity transitions from low to high frequencies and disrupted delta-centered cross-scale integration. Distinct coupling reconfiguration patterns emerged across resting states, indicating a systemic imbalance in multiscale integrative organization. Classification models built from statistically selected features performed consistently across Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbor, and Decision Tree algorithms, reaching a maximum accuracy of 85.71% with a balanced sensitivity-specificity profile. Convergent results across models further suggested the preliminary discriminative value of the proposed features within the present dataset. These findings provide a preliminary multiscale neurodynamic framework for EEG characterization in MDD and suggest that cross-scale integration differences may provide a quantitative basis for characterizing multiscale EEG dynamics in depression.

papers.title: Tirzepatide for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea: from apnea-hypopnea index reduction to cardiometabolic risk mitigation-a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a chronic respiratory disorder with nocturnal oxygen desaturation that is often associated with multisystemic sequelae such as hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, and increased morbidity and mortality. Obesity has been proposed as a modifiable risk factor; hence, the recent shift in focus to investigating anti-obesity medications for the management of OSA. Tirzepatide is the first U.S. FDA-approved pharmacotherapy for the treatment of moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity to be utilized in combination with low caloric intake and physical activity, given its prior success in managing type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity. This narrative review evaluates tirzepatide and the SURMOUNT-OSA trial program as the key contemporary anchors for the pharmacological treatment of OSA in adults with concurrent obesity. Because the randomized evidence base currently comprises a single pivotal trial program, the review centers on SURMOUNT-OSA and its prespecified endpoints along with post hoc analyses, supplemented by observational, modeling, and mechanistic studies. In the SURMOUNT-OSA program, tirzepatide produced randomized, placebo-controlled reductions in the apnea-hypopnea index, sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, and systemic inflammation. The program was designed around respiratory and metabolic endpoints rather than clinical events, so it cannot support conclusions about mortality, cardiovascular, or renal outcomes. Favorable signals for those events, including all-cause mortality, major adverse kidney events, and major adverse cardiovascular events, come only from nonrandomized observational cohorts and are best regarded as directional and exploratory rather than definitive. Tirzepatide may help frame OSA as a multifactorial and partially metabolically treatable disease and may represent a clinically meaningful expansion of treatment options alongside, rather than as a replacement for, established mechanical and procedural therapies. The available evidence is anchored in a single phase 3 trial program and limited by short follow-up and the absence of definitive comparative and long-term outcome data. Long-term durability of effect after discontinuation, generalizability beyond the SURMOUNT-OSA-eligible population, OSA-specific economic analysis, and head-to-head comparisons against CPAP remain the principal unsettled questions requiring dedicated long-term studies before firm clinical recommendations can be made.

papers.title: GmRVE8a, a circadian clock-associated gene, negatively regulates flowering and maturity in soybean.
papers.abstract: Precise regulation of flowering time and maturity is critical for achieving high and stable soybean yields, and the circadian clock plays a central role in coordinating these developmental transitions. Soybean is a typical short-day crop with a pronounced photoperiodic response; however, the molecular mechanisms linking circadian regulation to photoperiod-dependent flowering and maturity remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated genome-wide association analysis with deep learning approaches using 257 soybean germplasm accessions spanning 14 maturity groups and identified GmRVE8a, a homolog of the Arabidopsis circadian clock gene REVEILLE, as a strong candidate locus associated with soybean maturity across two field environments. Haplotype analysis demonstrated that accessions carrying the GmRVE8aH1 haplotype consistently flowered and matured significantly later than those carrying GmRVE8aH2. Functional validation revealed that knockout of GmRVE8a markedly accelerated flowering and maturity, whereas overexpression of GmRVE8a significantly delayed both processes. qRT-PCR assays further suggested that GmRVE8a may repress flowering and delay maturity by promoting the expression of GmFT4, a flowering-inhibitory member of the FT family, and is unlikely to act by directly regulating E1 expression. Collectively, our findings suggest GmRVE8a as a circadian clock-associated negative regulator of soybean flowering and maturity, and highlight it as a promising candidate for molecular breeding aimed at improving adaptation to diverse photoperiodic environments.
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology

papers.title: Dual-modal synaptic operation in a van der Waals heterostructure for emotion-inspired neuromorphic processing.
papers.abstract: Substantial progress has been made in artificial emotion-recognition systems; however, reproducing neurotransmitter-mediated emotional processing remains a major challenge for neuromorphic computing. In this study, we report bimodally modulated artificial synapses based on a van der Waals-stacked graphene quantum dot (GQD)/MoS2 heterostructure that integrates dopamine and optical stimuli for emotion-inspired neuromorphic processing. Incorporation of GQDs increases the ON-state current and dynamic range and improves relearning behavior and synaptic weight modulation. The GQD/MoS2 heterostructure exhibits dopamine-dependent electrical responses at concentrations of 1-5 nM and stable synaptic plasticity with retention maintained over the 1000 s measurement period. Optical stimulation in the presence of dopamine produces postsynaptic current (PSC) increases that exceed the additive expectation calculated from the individual optical-only and dopamine-only responses, supporting synergistic enhancement under the tested conditions. Device-informed facial emotion recognition simulations achieved an accuracy of 73.4% on the FER-2013 dataset using a convolutional neural network (CNN). Separately, classification of PSC-derived temporal signals using electroencephalography (EEG)-inspired processing achieved an accuracy of 76.6% with a support vector machine (SVM). These findings highlight the potential of this approach for affective computing and human-machine interaction.

papers.title: Community-based identification of poor sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with abdominal obesity using psychological and physical fitness indicators.
papers.abstract: Poor sleep quality, abdominal obesity, psychological symptoms, and declining physical function may cluster during midlife and later life, posing a multidimensional challenge to healthy aging. We aimed to develop and internally validate a community-oriented nomogram integrating readily obtainable psychological and physical fitness indicators to identify current poor sleep quality in community-dwelling middle-aged and older adults with abdominal obesity and to evaluate its added value over routinely available demographic and health information. This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed data from 212 adults aged ≥45 years with abdominal obesity assessed at a community health service center in Beijing, China. Poor sleep quality was defined as a Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) score >5. Ten candidate predictors were evaluated using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression with repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration measures, the Brier score, and decision curve analysis. Separate 1,000-resample bootstrap procedures assessed variable-selection stability and optimism in the performance of the fixed seven-predictor model. Among the 212 participants, 117 (55.2%) had poor sleep quality. The final model included age, the 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire, the 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale, grip strength, 30-s chair stand repetitions, chair sit-and-reach distance, and 2-min step count. The apparent AUC was 0.779 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.718-0.840]. After bootstrap optimism correction, the AUC, calibration slope, and Brier score were 0.751, 0.858, and 0.206, respectively. Compared with the routine-information model (apparent AUC, 0.648), the final model improved the AUC by 0.131 (95% CI, 0.050-0.213; p = 0.002) and showed greater theoretical net benefit across threshold probabilities of 13-80% in the development sample. The nomogram showed moderate internal performance and higher apparent performance than the routine-information model, although content overlap between PHQ-9 and PSQI may have inflated these estimates. Where psychological questionnaires and field-based fitness assessments are already available, it may support targeted sleep assessment in community healthy-aging programs. External validation is required before implementation in public health practice.

papers.title: Is There a Higher Risk of Obstructive Sleep Apnea among Individuals with Lower-Limb Compared to Those with Upper-Limb Lymphedema?
papers.abstract: Lymphedema, a chronic condition caused by impaired lymphatic drainage, can significantly affect patients' quality of life. While its impact on sleep quality is recognized, the association between lymphedema and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains underexplored. This study investigated whether individuals with lower-limb lymphedema (LLL) are at a higher risk of OSA compared to those with upper-limb lymphedema (ULL) and healthy controls. This cross-sectional study included 91 participants: 32 with ULL, 29 with LLL, and 30 healthy controls. Lymphedema was diagnosed based on excess volume (EV) and EV percentage (EVP) using standardized circumference measurements and the cylinder formula. Sleep quality and OSA risk were assessed using validated questionnaires: the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the 12-Item Short-Form Health Survey, version 2.0 (SF-12v2), the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), and the Snoring, Tiredness, Observed Apnea, High Blood Pressure, Body Mass Index, Age, Neck Circumference, and Gender (STOP-BANG) Questionnaire (SBQ). Participants with LLL exhibited significantly higher SBQ ( p = 0.022) and ESS ( p = 0.044) scores compared to those with ULL, indicating an elevated risk of OSA and daytime sleepiness. Furthermore, LLL patients had significantly lower physical ( p = 0.020) and mental ( p = 0.009) component scores on the SF-12v2, reflecting poorer health-related quality of life. Although PSQI scores were higher in the LLL group, the difference was not statistically significant. Regression analysis showed a significant association between EV and PSQI scores in the LLL group (adjusted p = 0.029), highlighting the impact of lymphedema severity on sleep quality. In this study, LLL was associated with a higher risk of OSA and greater sleep disturbances compared to ULL and controls.

papers.title: Sleep Management in Paralympic Sports: Knowledge, Monitoring Practices, and Perceived Barriers among Coaches and Healthcare Staff.
papers.abstract: Coaches and healthcare staff play a crucial role in disseminating knowledge about the importance of sleep to develop a precise balance between recovery and the demands imposed by sports training. To assess the knowledge on sleep, jet lag, and sleep hygiene (SH) among coaches and healthcare staff in Paralympic sports; 2) to identify whether the sleep of Paralympic athletes is monitored, and which instruments are commonly used; and 3) to identify the main barriers faced in sleep management. The present cross-sectional study was conducted with 60 coaches and healthcare staff who work in the preparation of elite Paralympic athletes. The participants filled out the Sleep Beliefs Scale and a structured questionnaire before traveling to the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games. Coaches and healthcare staff understand the importance of sleep for sports performance and recovery, but only 56% monitored their sleep. The most commonly used methods were subjective. Lack of adherence and commitment among Paralympic athletes (27%) and lack of training (19%) were the main barriers to sleep management. Coaches and healthcare staff are aware of the importance of sleep; however, educational programs are needed to improve the training of coaching and healthcare staff for efficient sleep management and to raise awareness among Paralympic athletes about the importance of sleep.

papers.title: Biopsychosocial Perioperative Care, Perioperative Stress, and Peripheral T-Cell Subset Recovery After Laparoscopic Hepatectomy for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Retrospective Propensity-Weighted Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Laparoscopic hepatectomy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) imposes substantial surgical and psychological stress, with potential neuroendocrine and immune consequences. Whether integrated biopsychosocial perioperative care is associated with differences across several perioperative domains remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association of a structured biopsychosocial (BPS) perioperative programme with psychological distress, stress hormones, cellular immunity, postoperative recovery, sleep, safety, and 18-month oncological outcomes after laparoscopic hepatectomy for HCC. This single-centre retrospective cohort included 343 consecutive patients treated between January 2022 and January 2025; 169 received BPS care plus conventional management and 174 received conventional care alone. Anxiety, depression, stress hormones, T-lymphocyte subsets, recovery, pain, opioid use, sleep, complications, recurrence, and survival were assessed longitudinally. Linear mixed-effects models and propensity-score overlap weighting with multivariable adjustment were used; time-to-event outcomes were analysed using Cox models. The anxiety (Self-Rating Anxiety Scale, SAS) and depression (Self-Rating Depression Scale, SDS) trajectories were prespecified as the co-primary outcomes. Propensity-score overlap weighting used covariates measured before programme allocation, and multiplicity was controlled within prespecified outcome families using the Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate procedure. After weighting, all measured covariates were balanced (maximum standardised mean difference 0.03). SAS and SDS trajectories favoured BPS care (group × time, both P<0.001), with adjusted discharge differences of -4.3 and -2.7 points, respectively. At postoperative day 7, the adjusted CD4+/CD8+ difference was +0.26 (95% CI 0.20-0.32). Length of stay was shorter by 1.1 days (95% CI -1.6 to -0.7), and 1-month PSQI was lower by 1.45 points (95% CI -1.78 to -1.12). Thirty-day complications, recurrence, and mortality were not statistically different. Peripheral-blood T-cell subset proportions index circulating composition and may not represent tissue or tumour-microenvironment antitumour immunity. After false-discovery-rate correction, all co-primary and secondary endpoints remained significant, whereas the safety and 18-month oncological endpoints did not. Structured BPS perioperative care was associated with favourable differences across several domains of postoperative recovery after laparoscopic hepatectomy for HCC. These findings support prospective multicentre randomised evaluation of integrated biopsychosocial care. The findings support integrated biopsychosocial care as a complement to, not a replacement for, established enhanced-recovery pathways.

papers.title: Cardiopulmonary Exercise Test-Derived Functional Indices Associated with Moderate-to-Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Young and Middle-Aged Adults.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with cardiovascular morbidity. However, exercise-related functional responses remain incompletely characterized in adults undergoing cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) for exercise prescription without established diseases affecting exercise capacity. We examined associations between CPET-derived indices and moderate-to-severe OSA, defined as an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥15 events/h. This single-center retrospective observational study included 104 adults aged 18-65 years who underwent overnight sleep monitoring with electroencephalographic recording and CPET for exercise prescription. Participants were classified into AHI ≥15 and AHI <15 events/h groups. Demographic characteristics, clinical variables, and CPET-derived indices were compared between groups. Heart rate recovery (HRR), peak oxygen pulse, and peak breathing reserve (BR) were examined in separate logistic regression models. Models were sequentially adjusted for sex, age, and body mass index (BMI). Among the 104 participants, 59 participants had AHI ≥15 events/h and 45 had AHI <15 events/h. The AHI ≥15 group had higher BMI and lower HRR, peak oxygen pulse (% predicted), and BR (all p < 0.001). After adjustment for sex, age, and BMI, higher HRR was associated with lower odds of AHI ≥15 events/h (OR = 0.745, 95% CI 0.640-0.867, p < 0.001). Higher BR was also associated with lower odds (OR = 0.923, 95% CI 0.878-0.971, p = 0.002). The adjusted association for peak oxygen pulse was not statistically significant. Lower HRR and BR were associated with moderate-to-severe OSA after adjustment for sex, age, and BMI in this selected cohort of young and middle-aged adults. Further prospective studies in independent cohorts are warranted to confirm these findings and clarify their potential clinical relevance.

papers.title: Remimazolam for Precision Sedation and Anaesthesia in Vulnerable Populations: A Narrative Review of Pharmacological Mechanisms, Stratified Clinical Evidence, and Individualised Perioperative Strategies.
papers.abstract: Sedation and anaesthesia in vulnerable populations are complicated by altered pharmacokinetics, variable pharmacodynamic sensitivity, and limited physiological reserve. The extent of these differences depends on the underlying condition, disease severity, comorbidity, and treatment setting. These issues are common in older adults, patients with obesity or obstructive sleep apnoea, organ dysfunction, cardiovascular vulnerability, critical illness, and neurological or psychiatric comorbidity. Conventional sedatives may be poorly tolerated in these settings. Propofol can cause hypotension and respiratory depression. Midazolam may lead to delayed recovery and accumulation. Dexmedetomidine may be limited by bradycardia and slow onset. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine that undergoes rapid carboxylesterase-mediated hydrolysis and can be antagonised with flumazenil. This narrative review examines its pharmacology, clinical evidence, and practical use across nine vulnerable populations. The synthesis prioritised population-specific clinical studies, pharmacokinetic studies, comparative trials, systematic reviews, and major guidelines. For short procedures, the most consistent evidence concerns older adults and haemodynamically vulnerable patients, in whom remimazolam has often been associated with less hypotension than propofol and faster recovery than midazolam. These findings are based mainly on short-term physiological and recovery outcomes. Evidence in mild to moderate hepatic or renal dysfunction is supportive but remains sparse in severe disease. Data for obesity or obstructive sleep apnoea, prolonged ICU sedation, paediatric care, obstetrics, and neurological or psychiatric vulnerability are limited or indirect. Remimazolam should therefore be considered according to the clinical objective, the expected duration and depth of sedation, opioid exposure, airway risk, and organ reserve. Its pharmacological advantages have not yet been shown to improve delirium, cognition, mechanical ventilation, functional recovery, or long-term safety. Further studies should focus on population-specific dosing models and patient-centred outcomes.

papers.title: Pathophysiology-guided nutritional strategies for persistent inflammation, immunosuppression, and catabolism syndrome: an immunometabolic perspective.
papers.abstract: Persistent inflammation, immunosuppression, and catabolism syndrome (PICS) is a phenotype of chronic critical illness characterized by unresolved inflammation, impaired immune competence, sustained catabolism, skeletal muscle loss, recurrent infections, and poor functional recovery. Although guideline-based nutritional support remains fundamental, persistent immunometabolic abnormalities may limit responsiveness to nutrient delivery and contribute to anabolic resistance, impaired substrate utilization, and defective tissue repair. This mini-review examines biological mechanisms limiting nutritional responsiveness in PICS and evaluates evidence for pathophysiology-guided nutritional strategies. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception through September 6, 2026, prioritizing English-language clinical guidelines, clinical studies, and mechanistic or translational evidence relevant to PICS, critical illness, nutritional responsiveness, and immunometabolic nutrition. We propose a framework addressing major barriers to recovery through strategies to restore anabolic responsiveness with protein, leucine, and rehabilitation; modulate inflammatory resolution and immune dysfunction with omega-3 fatty acids and arginine; optimize nutrient timing and circadian-metabolic regulation; and maintain a metabolic milieu conducive to nutrient utilization. Because direct interventional evidence in well-defined PICS populations remains limited, these strategies should complement rather than replace guideline-based nutritional support. The framework is conceptual and hypothesis-generating, and prospective PICS-specific studies incorporating biological stratification and clinically meaningful recovery outcomes are needed to determine its translational value.
keywords: persistent inflammation, immunosuppression, and catabolism syndrome (PICS)

papers.title: Comparison between Three-Night and Single-Night Actigraphic Sleep Assessment During Early Hospitalization.
papers.abstract: To determine whether a single-night actigraphic sleep assessment during early hospitalization can approximate a 3-night average and characterize inpatient sleep- and rest-activity rhythm. In the present multicenter, cross-sectional study conducted in 7 Czech hospitals, 64 inpatients underwent wrist actigraphic monitoring during the first 3 nights of hospitalization. Actual sleep time, sleep latency, mobile time, sleep efficiency, fragmentation index and average light exposure were analyzed. First-night values were compared with 3-night means using the Wilcoxon test. Individual-level agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman analysis. Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis (NPCRA) variables were reported descriptively. The 3-night mean sleep duration was 342 ± 83 minutes, with reduced sleep efficiency and increased fragmentation. No significant differences were observed between first-night values and 3-night averages for actual sleep time, mobile time, sleep efficiency, fragmentation index or average light exposure. Agreement was good for these parameters (ICC_single ≈ 0.71-0.75), whereas sleep latency showed lower reliability (ICC_single = 0.51). The Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated no systematic bias, with up to 6.3% of observations outside the 95% limits of agreement for most parameters and 9.4% for sleep latency. The NPCRA suggested preserved relative amplitude but fragmented rest-activity rhythm. Single-night actigraphy provides reliable estimates for most inpatient sleep parameters and may represent a pragmatic alternative to multi-night monitoring in acute hospital settings. Sleep latency is less stable and may require repeated assessment.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Consistency of Peri-ictal Hemodynamic Findings Revealed by Capturing More Than 3 Seizures Using 1.5-Tesla Pseudo-continuous Arterial Spin Labeling Magnetic Resonance Perfusion Imaging with Triple Post-labeling Delays: Report of 3 Cases.
papers.abstract: In the pathophysiological diagnosis of seizures in neuro-emergencies, the usefulness of arterial spin labeling perfusion imaging, which can be performed 24 hr a day, 7 days a week, in capturing peri-ictal hyperperfusion has been reported as a means of compensating for the limitations of electroencephalography, which is available only during regular hours. Herein, we retrospectively evaluated the consistency of arterial spin labeling findings in conjunction with electroencephalography findings in 3 patients with 3 or more seizures. Patients 1 and 2 both experienced 3 seizures and were transported outside of regular hours. On arterial spin labeling, consistent peri-ictal hyperperfusion was observed in the right posterior quadrant with a close anatomical relationship to the epileptogenic lesion in Patient 1 and in the right occipitotemporal lobe without an identifiable epileptogenic lesion in Patient 2. Subsequent electroencephalography failed to reveal any paroxysmal discharges. Patient 3 experienced 4 seizures. Electroencephalography performed immediately after the third seizure demonstrated ictal discharges in the right frontal region, while the other electroencephalography recordings showed paroxysmal discharges and rhythmic slow waves in the same region. In arterial spin labeling, hyperperfusion was observed in the right frontal lobe only during the second seizure, whereas hypoperfusion was observed in the same region during the other seizures. This pattern was likely attributable to an early transition from ictal hyperperfusion to postictal or interictal hypoperfusion, and was therefore considered a consistent arterial spin labeling finding. Although consistent peri-ictal hyperperfusion is commonly observed on arterial spin labeling, hypoperfusion may also be observed; as such, comprehensive evaluation, including electroencephalography findings, is required for accurate diagnosis.

papers.title: Examining sources of variability in repeated testing of the reward positivity and P300 ERP components.
papers.abstract: Event-related potentials (ERPs) provide millisecond-resolution measurements of cognitive and affective processes, making them a foundational tool in human neuroscience research. A clear understanding of their reliability, stability, and sensitivity is therefore essential for interpreting experimental results with confidence, particularly in multi-task protocols where several ERPs are measured in sequence. The present study examined three sources of variability for two widely used components, the P300 and the rewards positivity: test-retest reliability, systematic amplitude changes across repeated measurements, and order effects. Twenty-six adults completed five cognitive assessments distributed over approximately 2 h, with each assessment containing a visual oddball task and a two-armed bandit task; task order was independently randomized within each assessment. Reliability was quantified using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), changes across repeated assessments were tested with linear mixed-effects models, and order effects were evaluated using mixed-effects models accounting for repeated observations within participants. The P300 demonstrated excellent reliability across all five assessments (ICC = 0.91). The rewards positivity showed a clear divergence between conditional and difference-wave measures: the difference wave was moderately reliable (ICC = 0.52), while the underlying win (0.92) and loss (0.92) waves demonstrated excellent reliability. Rewards positivity amplitude showed no evidence of a linear change across assessments, whereas P300 amplitude increased systematically across the testing period. No evidence of order effects was observed for either component, indicating that task order did not meaningfully influence ERP amplitude within sessions of this length. Together, these findings characterize the reliability and time-related variability of the P300 and rewards positivity during repeated within-session testing and provide practical guidance for multi-task EEG protocols.

papers.title: Synergistic contributions of periodic and aperiodic cortical activity to motor recovery prediction after stroke.
papers.abstract: Functional motor recovery in chronic stroke can be promoted by intensive exercise aided by neurotechnology, yet reliable physiological markers to predict recovery remain limited. Scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used in clinical routines, but conventional band-power metrics conflate oscillatory (periodic) and broadband (aperiodic) activity, limiting their interpretability. Here, we tested whether EEG spectral profiles predict motor recovery in chronic stroke. Resting-state EEG (1 min) was recorded at admission and discharge using a portable system (N = 41) and parameterized with a spectral decomposition model. Parameters were examined in relation to motor improvement, as indexed by gain in a clinical score, and used to construct a prediction model. Ipsilesional periodic activity at the individual alpha frequency (IAF) significantly increased after rehabilitation (P = 0.024) and correlated with motor improvement (r = 0.39, P = 0.010). A stepwise regression model identified higher IAF peaks, steeper aperiodic slopes, and their interaction as predictors of recovery (Severe group: R 2 = 0.53, P = 0.003; balanced accuracy = 88%). The model outperformed a delta-alpha ratio-based approach commonly used in stroke prognosis. These findings indicate that the synergistic interaction between periodic and aperiodic activity provides a mechanistically meaningful and clinically relevant biomarker of residual plasticity, supporting individualized rehabilitation strategies in chronic stroke.

papers.title: Tonmya (Sublingual Cyclobenzaprine HCl) in Fibromyalgia and Chronic Pain: A Psychopharmacologic Perspective - Brief Commentary.
papers.abstract: To review the psychopharmacologic profile of Tonmya (cyclobenzaprine HCl sublingual tablets), FDA-approved August 15, 2025, as the first new fibromyalgia therapy in over 15 years, and provide practical guidance for integration in cases with psychiatric comorbidity. Tonmya targets sleep disruption, pain, and fatigue via receptor antagonism (5-HT2A serotonergic, α1-adrenergic, H1-histaminergic, M1-muscarinic), with sublingual delivery reducing daytime sedation. Phase 3 RESILIENT trial data showed significant pain reduction (p < 0.0001, effect size 0.38 at week 14), sleep/fatigue improvements, and favorable tolerability. Psychiatrists and collaborators can use Tonmya adjunctively in fibromyalgia with mood/somatic features, emphasizing patient selection, documentation, monitoring, and multidisciplinary care to minimize risks and enhance outcomes in psychosomatic pain syndromes.

papers.title: Augmented cardiac growth hormone signaling in circadian-disrupted cardiomyopathy.
papers.abstract: Circadian disruption, including rotating shift work, social jet lag, and chronic sleep disturbance, is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and may promote cardiac remodeling. The molecular mechanisms connecting clock disruption to structural heart disease remain incompletely defined. This minireview advances the hypothesis that the growth hormone, GH, axis is an underrecognized endocrine mediator. GH secretion is time dependent, with most daily secretion occurring during early nocturnal sleep-in humans. Cardiomyocytes express GH receptors, and GH can activate Janus kinase 2, signal transducer and activator of transcription 5, phosphoinositide 3 kinase and Akt, and mitogen activated protein kinase and extracellular signal regulated kinase pathways that influence cardiac growth and metabolism. We propose that the cardiomyocyte molecular clock restricts GH responsiveness to circadian phases. REV ERBα is a plausible component of this restraint, but direct cardiomyocyte evidence is lacking. Circadian disruption may increase or mistime myocardial GH signaling, promoting hypertrophy, fibrosis, and metabolic inflexibility. The strongest support comes from cardiomyocyte specific Bmal1 deficient mice, which show increased GH induced cardiac STAT5 phosphorylation, increased cardiac Igf1 expression, and remodeling. Reduction of GH receptor gene dosage partially attenuates this phenotype, supporting a causal contribution of cardiac GH signaling. Nevertheless, genetic clock ablation is not equivalent to environmental circadian misalignment in shift work or chronic sleep disruption. We critically evaluate the components of this proposed clock-GH-heart axis, identify unresolved questions, and outline experiments and chronopharmacological strategies to test whether restoring temporal control of GH signaling can prevent pathological remodeling while preserving physiological GH action.

papers.title: Sleep disorders and cardiovascular diseases.
papers.abstract: Although the health benefits of good sleep have been recognized for centuries, many people continue to struggle with sleep disorders triggered by many factors. Despite numerous studies on sleep disorders, a comprehensive understanding of their risk factors and potential mechanisms remains elusive. This review critically examines how circadian desynchrony acts as the primary driver linking sleep disorders and circadian clock dysfunction to dysregulated lipid metabolism and chronic vascular inflammation, ultimately accelerating atherosclerosis, and mainly focuses on the interplay of sleep-induced metabolic issues with the genetic and environmental factors that alter sleep patterns. Maintaining optimal sleep rhythm, quality, and timing is essential to decrease the risk of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases.

papers.title: Risk Factor Profiles and Clinical Outcomes: A 6-Month Longitudinal Study on Rehospitalization Rates in Patients with Chronic Heart Failure.
papers.abstract: To evaluate rehospitalization rates and identify modifiable risk factors in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients enrolled in an optimal management and treatment program. A prospective cross-sectional study with longitudinal follow-up was conducted on 163 patients diagnosed with CHF patients (Framingham criteria) at an international hospital model in Vietnam from January 2022 to November 2023. Clinical, behavioral, and comorbid factors were analyzed over 6 months. The program demonstrated high efficacy with a low 6-month rehospitalization rate of 9.82%. Statistical analysis revealed significant correlations between rehospitalization and male gender (p<0.01), alcohol consumption (p<0.05), smoking (p<0.05), elevated heart rate (p<0.001), and NYHA functional class (p<0.05). Key comorbidities including coronary heart disease (p<0.01), sinus tachycardia (p < 0.001), atrial fibrillation (p<0.01), and sleep disorders were also significantly associated with readmission (p<0.05). Optimizing CHF outcomes requires a comprehensive intervention strategy targeting both modifiable lifestyle factors and underlying clinical comorbidities like sleep disorders.

papers.title: Adult-Onset Limb-Girdle Phenotype Associated With a Homozygous PYROXD1 Variant: The Case of a North African Family.
papers.abstract: Mutations in the pyridine nucleotide-disulfide oxide reductase domain-containing protein 1 (PYROXD1) gene are characteristically linked to early-onset congenital myofibrillar myopathy, typically presenting with generalized weakness, hypotonia, and respiratory insufficiency in infancy or early childhood. However, emerging evidence suggests phenotypic heterogeneity. We report the case of a 45-year-old Tunisian woman, born to non-consanguineous parents, who presented with a slowly progressive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD) phenotype; her older brother, subsequently confirmed to carry the same homozygous variant, had a similar but more severe clinical history of proximal weakness. The patient's symptoms began at age 17 with running difficulties, progressing by age 35 to difficulty rising from a seated position and climbing stairs, and by age 45 to exertional dyspnea, dysphagia, and sleep-disordered breathing. Physical examination revealed a high-arched palate, scoliosis, joint hypermobility, limited ankle dorsiflexion, palatal weakness, and mild neck flexion weakness alongside a proximal-dominant limb-girdle pattern of weakness. Her brother showed a matching but more severe phenotype starting at age 12. Electrodiagnostic studies demonstrated normal nerve conduction and a non-irritable myopathy; serum creatine kinase was entirely normal, and pulmonary function testing revealed a restrictive ventilatory defect with mild obstructive sleep apnea on polysomnography. Clinical exome sequencing confirmed a pathogenic homozygous c.464A>G (p.Asn155Ser) mutation in the PYROXD1 gene in both affected siblings, with both parents confirmed as unaffected heterozygous carriers. This represents the first molecularly confirmed family with PYROXD1-related myopathy in Tunisia and North Africa, and only the second family identified across the African continent; a single unrelated Tunisian case harboring the same variant has also recently been reported. This case expands the known clinical spectrum of PYROXD1 variants to include adult-onset LGMD-like presentations with respiratory and bulbar involvement, emphasizes the diagnostic utility of recognizing associated dysmorphic features (scoliosis, high-arched palate, nasal speech, and joint hypermobility), and highlights the pivotal role of comprehensive genomic testing in atypical adult myopathies.

papers.title: Anti-correlation time-frequency synergy and dual-granularity fusion for sleep stage classification.
papers.abstract: Automated sleep stage classification is crucial for diagnosing sleep disorders and evaluating sleep quality. Single-channel EEG sleep staging using central electrodes has garnered significant interest due to its ability to detect a higher number of sleep spindles and its cost-effectiveness. Nevertheless, several challenges remain, such as the neglect of interdependencies among features, reduced model sensitivity to the dispersion across features, potential information leakage during the learning of transition rules, and class imbalance. To address these challenges, this study specifically designs an automatic sleep staging network based on single-channel EEG. The network incorporates a multi-branch feature extraction module, which captures negatively correlated frequency features that exhibit significant variations during sleep transitions and promotes synergistic complementarity. Furthermore, a dual-granularity residual attention mechanism is employed to perform adaptive fusion along both temporal and channel dimensions based on statistical measures such as the mean and standard deviation. The causal transition-aware network ensures temporal consistency while facilitating effective learning of transition rules. The focal loss function is utilized to counteract class imbalance.
