Using AI to help diagnose OSA can reduce wait times and lead to earlier diagnosis and treatment. Big data can allow for detailed analysis of patient characteristics using AI and can aid in sub-categorizing patients. AI is an important tool that could be used to augment sleep providers to: improve workflow, bridge the gap between symptom onset and diagnosis, and facilitate a precision care approach to our patients.

papers.title: Automated Sleep Staging: Are Algorithms Ready for the Clinic?
papers.abstract: Sleep staging is an important tool to diagnose sleep disorders but can be a time-intensive process. The development of artificial intelligence-based automated sleep staging programs can alleviate barriers to scoring by improving efficiency and achieving standardized results. However, careful implementation of these programs is needed to ensure appropriate use. Artificial intelligence models can generate unreliable clinical results if models are not trained on heterogenous data that represent both common and infrequent sleep disorders. It is essential to recognize the limitations of artificial intelligence-based scoring prior to integration in clinical workflows to promote meaningful improvements in care delivery.

papers.title: Sleep Data Repositories in Practice: Signal Processing, Quality Control, and Artificial Intelligence Integration.
papers.abstract: Realizing the scientific and clinical potential of large-scale sleep data repositories requires rigorous technical infrastructure for signal processing, quality control, and artificial intelligence (AI) integration. This article addresses the practical implementation steps that follow repository architecture and data ingestion. We outline strategies for linking sleep study data with longitudinal electronic health records, including deterministic and probabilistic matching, temporal alignment, and approaches to handling missing linkages and incomplete clinical data. Finally, we discuss emerging directions, including wearable data integration, federated and privacy-preserving learning, precision medicine applications, and regulatory and health equity considerations essential to responsible repository-scale AI deployment.

papers.title: Building a Sleep Data Repository: Architecture, Data Sources, and Governance.
papers.abstract: Large-scale sleep data repositories are critical for precision sleep medicine, artificial intelligence-driven research, and population-level studies of sleep disorders. This article presents a practical framework for building scalable repositories. Key components include data intake and processing, centralized storage, external data integration, and secure study environments. We discuss emerging data sources such as polysomnography, home sleep apnea testing, and consumer wearables, along with requirements for data standardization, including European Data Format parsing, channel harmonization, and metadata validation. The framework also highlights governance principles for compliant data use across multiple regulatory environments, providing guidance for developing secure and scalable sleep data infrastructure.

papers.title: Data Standards and Benchmarking: Toward Reproducible Artificial Intelligence in Sleep Medicine.
papers.abstract: This review outlines the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence in sleep medicine, particularly highlighting the role of machine learning in analyzing inherently digital polysomnography data. While machine learning offers time-saving automated scoring, the field struggles with reproducibility and generalizability across varying clinical settings due to domain shift. To establish a standardized framework, this text emphasizes the utilization of public datasets, open models, and common benchmarks. In addition, it details advanced algorithmic approaches, such as domain adaptation and generalization, alongside foundational best practices in signal preprocessing and data splitting to ensure robust performance and prevent data leakage.

papers.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence: Building Trust in the Sleep Clinic.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied in sleep medicine, where complex multimodal data create opportunities for automation and clinical decision support. However, many high-performing AI models remain black-boxes, limiting transparency, trust, and safe clinical adoption. Explainable AI (XAI) addresses this gap by providing insight into model behavior, helping identify bias and assess unreliable predictions. XAI also supports emerging regulatory expectations for transparency and human oversight. This review summarizes key XAI principles, methods, limitations, regulatory considerations, and clinical applications in sleep medicine, including sleep staging and sleep apnea diagnostics, emphasizing AI as a tool to augment, rather than replace, clinical expertise.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Sleep Medicine: A Primer for Clinicians.
papers.abstract: As the opening article in this Sleep Medicine Clinics issue on artificial intelligence (AI) in sleep medicine, this primer addresses the limited exposure most sleep clinicians have to the principles behind these tools. Adopting AI outputs without understanding how models are trained, validated, and tested may compromise clinical decision-making. This review covers fundamental AI concepts, methodological limitations, and clinical integration. It also addresses how AI sleep medicine research should be appraised through regulatory principles and structured critical appraisal frameworks.

papers.title: Evolving indications for metabolic and bariatric surgery.
papers.abstract: This chapter addresses patient selection for metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) in the modern obesity care landscape, where anti-obesity medications (AOMs) such as semaglutide and tirzepatide have changed the clinical decision-making framework. We organize the evidence around four questions a clinician actually asks: who qualifies under current guidelines, who benefits most and from which procedure, who is poorly served by surgery, and when pharmacotherapy is the better answer. We review the evolution of indications from the 1991 NIH Consensus Conference through the 2022 ASMBS/IFSO joint guidelines, with attention to the randomized evidence supporting expanded indications at BMI 30-34.9 kg/m² with type 2 diabetes. We then examine outcomes by patient phenotype, including type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, obstructive sleep apnea, heart failure, transplant candidacy, polycystic ovary syndrome, pregnancy planning, and elevated cancer risk. We identify populations for whom surgery carries an unfavorable risk-benefit profile, including patients with advanced perioperative risk, decompensated cirrhosis, untreated psychiatric illness, active substance use, or inability to maintain long-term nutritional follow-up. Finally, we provide a comparative analysis of MBS and modern AOMs across cardiometabolic outcomes, with attention to the methodological limitations of current cohort comparisons and the role of combination and sequential strategies. The chapter concludes that the two modalities are converging on a complementary framework in which patient phenotype, not BMI alone, determines the right intervention.

papers.title: Endoscopic bariatric and metabolic therapies.
papers.abstract: Obesity remains one of the most urgent global health challenges, driving substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare expenditure. Although lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, and bariatric surgery form the traditional pillars of treatment, each has important limitations. Lifestyle therapy often produces transient weight loss, newer anti-obesity medications are effective but limited by cost and tolerability, and bariatric surgery-while the most durable intervention-continues to reach only a small fraction of eligible patients. Endoscopic bariatric and metabolic therapies (EBMTs) have emerged to bridge this gap, offering incisionless, organ-sparing interventions with efficacy exceeding lifestyle treatment alone and risk profiles generally lower than surgery. Intragastric balloons provide temporary gastric volume occupancy and achieve modest total body weight loss, though durability is limited after device removal. Endoscopic gastric remodeling techniques, particularly endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG), offer greater and more durable weight loss, with meaningful improvement in obesity-related comorbidities including diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, and metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease. Revisional procedures such as revisional ESG and transoral outlet reduction (TORe) address weight regain after sleeve gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, respectively, providing effective lower-risk alternatives to revisional surgery. Emerging small bowel therapies, including duodenal-jejunal bypass liners and duodenal mucosal ablation platforms, target foregut physiology and insulin resistance, with particular promise for patients with type 2 diabetes and poor glycemic control. With increasing emphasis on chronic, multimodal obesity management, this chapter informs healthcare professionals on the current evidence for primary and revisional EBMTs and how they may fit into the advancing paradigm of individualized obesity care.

papers.title: Diagnosis and evaluation of obesity for therapeutic selection.
papers.abstract: Obesity is increasingly recognized as a chronic, heterogeneous, and multifactorial disease that requires a more detailed diagnostic approach than traditional weight-based classification alone. Although body mass index (BMI) remains widely used for initial screening, it does not adequately capture adipose tissue distribution, metabolic phenotype, or organ-level complications. Consequently, reliance on BMI in isolation may lead to both underecognition of high-risk individuals and overclassification of others. This chapter presents a structured framework to guide clinicians and other professionals interested in obesity care in the diagnostic evaluation of obesity and the selection of individualized therapeutic strategies. The approach combines anthropometric measures with clinical staging systems and evaluation of obesity-related complications, consistent with the shift toward an adiposity-based disease model. The Edmonton Obesity Staging System (EOSS), the 2024 European Association for the Study of Obesity (EASO) criteria, and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinology (AACE) adiposity-based chronic disease (ABCD) model are reviewed as complementary approaches that move beyond BMI-centric definitions. Particular emphasis is placed on matching pharmacologic therapy with the predominant complication profile, such as type 2 diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, obstructive sleep apnea, and sarcopenic obesity. In this context, therapeutic decision-making is informed not only by the degree of excess adiposity but also by its clinical consequences. The chapter concludes with practical considerations for longitudinal monitoring and long-term disease management.

papers.title: The role of physical activity in the management of obesity.
papers.abstract: Physical activity is a crucial component of overall health and physical function. It is also associated with obesity management in a variety of ways. Physical activity can impact weight directly by burning calories during and after movement. In addition, its role in building or conserving muscle mass has the potential to affect calories burned at rest. Physical activity and decreased sedentary time may indirectly impact weight by regulating calories consumed. This impact is highly variable but potential mediators include appetite regulation, sleep, mood regulation, and other psychological factors. In the current era of obesity management, characterized by obesity management medications (OMMs) and metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS), physical activity may have a diminishing role in creating energy deficits. Instead, physical activity should be considered in the context of treating the broader condition of obesity. Obesity is associated with a number of health conditions that decrease longevity and quality of life. Physical activity, even without substantial weight loss, prevents and treats many of these same conditions. Weight loss and physical activity can impact each other in a bi-directional way, with weight loss making movement easier and more enjoyable, and physical activity improving energy and self-efficacy that can be used to manage the nutritional side of weight management. Practitioners should avoid generic exercise prescriptions for obesity and instead complete comprehensive assessments to guide individualized treatments. These treatments should incorporate patient values, utilize empirically supported behavioral principles including self-monitoring, consider technology, and be collaborative in nature.

papers.title: Navigating the 'known unknowns' and grey zone of pacing for profound cardioinhibitory vasovagal syncope.
Combined structural and functional assessment of the ophthalmic trigeminal pathway in healthy adults: a feasibility study with preliminary reference data.
Clip-to-trial: EEG-based decoding network with long short-term self-attention for DRDS recognition.
papers.abstract: Dynamic random-dot stereograms (DRDS) elicit stereoscopic perception associated with high-level binocular visual processing, which can be decoded from EEG signals. However, existing EEG-based approaches predominantly rely on clip-level learning, leading to feature-label misalignment and limited modeling of trial-level spatiotemporal dependencies. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a clip-to-trial long short-term self-attention network (C2T-LSTSA) for EEG-based DRDS recognition. The proposed method first extracts discriminative spatiotemporal features from EEG clips using a multi-scale local feature extraction module. A trial-level feature reconstruction module is then introduced to explicitly map clip-level representations into semantically consistent trial-level features. Furthermore, a long short-term self-attention module is employed to jointly model local temporal dependencies within each reconstructed trial representation and global dependencies among multiple reconstructed trial representations derived from the same original EEG trial. Extensive experiments on three EEG datasets collected from strabismus patients demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches under both subject-dependent and subject-independent evaluation protocols, indicating its effectiveness and robustness for objective assessment of stereoscopic visual function. The reference datasets are available at https://github.com/YANGeeg/TJU-SRD-datasets and the code is at https://github.com/wu860898-design/C2T-LSTSA.

papers.title: Central nervous system involvement, sequelae, and prognostic markers in children with severe hand-foot-and-mouth disease: A multicenter cohort study across four Chinese cities.
papers.abstract: Approximately 10% of severe hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD) cases develop post-recovery sequelae such as language and cognitive impairments, posing major social and family burdens. However, large-scale evidence on long-term outcomes is limited. This multicenter cohort study retrospectively analyzed hospitalized HFMD cases between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2023, in four cities (Zhengzhou, Changchun, Xi'an, and Zhoukou). Among 25,536 medical records, all severe HFMD inpatients were identified, and mild HFMD inpatients from the same period were randomly selected as controls at a 1:1 ratio, resulting in 1,909 patients in each group. Sequelae were assessed through long-term follow-up, and potential prognostic markers were examined using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. The result showed that severe HFMD was associated with a significantly higher risk of long-term sequelae compared with mild cases, including motor disorders, epilepsy, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, tic disorders, language disorders, developmental delays, psychiatric disorders, intellectual disabilities, and social impairments. Independent predictors of sequelae were peak fever, feeding mode, serum creatinine, serum sodium, and complement C3 levels, which together provided effective prediction of the 6-year cumulative risk. Abnormal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and electroencephalography (EEG) findings during the acute phase were strongly correlated with subsequent sequelae. Furthermore, learning disabilities were more common among patients with severe HFMD, further highlighting the potential long-term neurological and neurodevelopmental burden of the disease. Together, these findings underscore the importance of long-term follow-up and further research to improve early identification of children at risk and inform strategies to reduce the long-term effect of HFMD.

papers.title: Sleep-stage dynamics in depression: Altered stage distribution and N2 persistence, with incremental information from distribution entropy beyond demographic and subjective clinical measures.
papers.abstract: Depression involves sleep complaints not fully captured by polysomnography. We examined whether objective sleep-stage dynamics were associated with documented depressive disorder after accounting for apnea and sedative use, whether associations persisted after anxiety adjustment, and whether distribution entropy added information beyond self-reports. In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study of patients undergoing clinically indicated polysomnography (n = 303; 139 with and 164 without documented depressive disorder; non-depressed clinical comparators, not healthy controls), nine objective features, selected from 678 candidates by exploratory screening, were tested in progressively adjusted logistic models with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate control across nine features. Sensitivity analyses addressed anxiety, sleep quality, and medication classes. After adjustment for demographics, night-time sedative use, and apnea-hypopnea index, lower sleep-stage distribution entropy (OR 0.63), longer N2 bout duration (OR 1.52), lower total transition rate (OR 0.66), and lower N2 → N1 transition probability (OR 0.55) remained associated with documented depressive disorder (all q < 0.05). Directions were preserved in the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI; n = 195) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) ≥15 exclusion (n = 241) samples; in the latter, none remained FDR-significant (q = 0.054-0.106). In this sleep-clinic sample, adding entropy to a demographic-subjective model increased apparent AUC from 0.78 to 0.81; optimism-corrected ΔAUC 0.034 (point estimate). Conditional on covariates, documented depressive disorder was associated with altered sleep-stage distribution and continuity-related dynamics, including greater N2 persistence. Residual medication and indication confounding cannot be excluded; attenuation after anxiety adjustment limits specificity. These exploratory findings require replication.

papers.title: "You Get a Detention if You Get Out of Your Chair": Adolescents' Experiences of a School-Based Movement Intervention.
papers.abstract: School-based interventions are commonly used to promote physical activity and reduce sedentary behavior among adolescents. This study explored adolescents' perceptions and experiences of the implementation of the TransformUs Secondary program, including how it was integrated into the school day and perceived changes in physical activity, sedentary behavior, sleep, and well-being. This qualitative study was part of the TransformUs Secondary effectiveness trial conducted in Victoria, Australia. TransformUs Secondary is a whole-school intervention to promote physical activity and reduce sedentary behavior through active lessons, active breaks, peer support, teacher professional learning, and environmental modifications. Focus groups were conducted with students from 4 intervention schools following the intervention. Students in years 7-10 (aged 12-16 y) were recruited by convenience sampling. Students' experiences of physically active learning, sedentary behavior, sleep, well-being, and perceptions of the program were explored. Discussions were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Twenty-three adolescents (mean age = 13 y, 56.5% male) participated across 4 focus groups from 3 schools. Students described limited visibility of the intervention. Active breaks and movement-based activities were perceived as dependent on teacher support. Traditional classroom norms prioritizing seated learning, strict behavioral rules, and classroom layouts were perceived barriers. Nevertheless, students expressed positive attitudes toward physical activity and its benefits for well-being, focus, and social connection. Most students perceived little change in their behavior, sleep, or well-being during the intervention period. Embedding movement within secondary schools may require addressing systemic barriers rather than relying on individual teacher initiative alone.

papers.title: A Systems-Based Approach to Preventing Recurrent Injuries in Obese Adolescents: Integrating Strength, Technology, Recovery, and Lifestyle Factors.
papers.abstract: This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence and propose an integrated conceptual framework for preventing recurrent musculoskeletal injuries in obese adolescents. A narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature was conducted across multiple scientific databases, focusing on published studies that examined injury risk, reinjury, physical training, recovery, and lifestyle factors in adolescents with overweight or obesity. The evidence indicates that obese adolescents exhibit reduced relative strength, impaired neuromuscular control, altered movement mechanics, and compromised recovery capacity, all of which contribute to elevated reinjury risk. Strength and neuromuscular training emerge as foundational components for enhancing load tolerance and movement efficiency. Technology-based monitoring tools offer opportunities to individualize load progression and detect early maladaptation, while recovery processes such as sleep and fatigue management critically influence tissue adaptation. Lifestyle and behavioral factors further shape injury risk by affecting physical activity patterns, adherence, and recovery behaviors. Preventing recurrent musculoskeletal injuries in obese adolescents requires a systems-based, multidimensional approach that extends beyond traditional rehabilitation paradigms. Integrating physical training, monitoring technologies, recovery strategies, and lifestyle considerations within a unified framework may improve injury resilience and support sustainable participation in physical activity.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Different Types of Physical Activity Interventions for Enhancing Sleep Quality in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Poor sleep quality is common among older adults, affecting health and well-being. Physical activity is a promising nonpharmacological option, but the comparative effects of different exercise types remain unclear. This study compared various physical activity interventions on subjective sleep quality in older adults through network meta-analysis. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus identified eligible evaluating physical activity effects on sleep quality in adults aged ≥60 years. Sleep quality was measured using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Interventions were categorized as aerobic, resistance, balance, flexibility, or multicomponent training. Bayesian network meta-analysis estimated mean differences (MDs) with 95% credible intervals (CrI). A total of 39 studies involving 3198 participants met the inclusion criteria. Balance training showed the greatest estimated improvement (MD = -2.58; 95% CrI, -3.32 to -1.83), followed by flexibility (MD = -1.70; 95% CrI, -3.90 to 0.50), aerobic (MD = -1.47; 95% CrI, -2.43 to -0.50), multicomponent (MD = -1.30; 95% CrI, -2.44 to -0.18), and resistance training (MD = -1.17; 95% CrI, -2.19 to -0.15), all of which were significantly superior to control. Flexibility training (n = 2) demonstrated a relatively large estimated effect (MD = 1.70; 95% CrI, -0.50 to 3.90), although the result did not reach statistical significance. Balance training demonstrated the greatest potential for improving sleep quality in older adults and ranked highest in the network meta-analysis. Aerobic, multicomponent, and resistance exercise also showed significant benefits compared with control.

papers.title: Psychomotor vigilance is multidimensional: evidence from index network analysis, parameter review, and neuroimaging.
papers.abstract: The Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) is widely used to assess vigilance, with interpretation shaped by experimental parameters, index definitions, and neurophysiological context. This review examines stimulus modality, task duration, and interstimulus interval, then considers the calculation and use of PVT indices. An exploratory network analysis of 15 indices in 678 participants examines a three-group descriptive framework comprising Stable, Overall, and Control indices. Electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging findings relate vigilance to waking oscillations, EEG network stability, preceding sleep physiology, and functional brain connectivity. Multimodal assessment offers opportunities to refine vigilance monitoring in sleep medicine, fatigue research, and occupational settings such as aviation and shift work.

papers.title: Associations between objective sleep outcomes and performance on neurocognitive tests used to guide sport-related concussion diagnosis and management: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Examine whether objective sleep outcomes associate with cognitive performance assessed by tools (i.e., Sport Concussion Assessment Tool [SCAT5]; Immediate Post-Concussion Assessment Testing [ImPACT]) used to support clinical decision-making for sports-related concussion. Participants' (n = 20) sleep was monitored for 4-5 nights with a dry-electroencephalography device prior to baseline SCAT5 and ImPACT testing. Sleep measures included total sleep time, sleep efficiency, and sleep stage proportions (N1%, N2%, N3%, REM%). Cognitive outcomes included SCAT5 orientation, immediate memory, concentration, and delayed recall, and ImPACT verbal memory, visual memory, visual motor speed and reaction time. Spearman's rank correlations revealed REM% was strongly correlated with subsequent SCAT5 Concentration score (ρ = 0.71, p < 0.001). Exploratory regression indicated mean REM% was predictive of SCAT5 Concentration (β = 0.49; 95%CI = 0.14, 0.85; OR = 1.64; p = 0.006). SCAT5 Concentration performance was associated with prior REM%. Significant REM sleep loss may confound subsequent SCAT Concentration testing; however, more research is needed to elucidate any potential effects on overall SCAT neurocognitive testing outcomes. When interpreting SCAT neurocognitive outcomes, clinicians should consider whether players have experienced significant/major pre-test sleep disturbances.

papers.title: Delayed-Release Methylphenidate in Pediatric Patients With Early Morning Sleep Inertia and Brain Fog: A Case Series and Review of the Literature.
papers.abstract: Early morning sleep inertia and brain fog can become severe and functionally disabling symptoms in delayed sleep phase syndrome and other sleep disorders, including narcolepsy. Standard treatments including melatonin, bright light therapy, behavioral sleep-wake scheduling, and daytime wake-promoting agents yield incomplete responses in a substantial proportion of patients. We conducted an institutional review board-approved retrospective chart review of 15 patients with refractory early morning sleep inertia and brain fog treated with nightly delayed-release methylphenidate. Nine pediatric patients (ages 13-17) with complete preintervention and postintervention Likert scores were included for analysis. The cohort included nine patients with diagnoses including delayed sleep phase syndrome (n = 7), narcolepsy type 1 (n = 1), and narcolepsy type 2 (n = 1). Common comorbidities included attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, major depressive disorder, and generalized anxiety disorder. Median early morning Likert scores improved from 6/7 (range 5-7) to 2/7 (range 1-4) postintervention, with 7 of the 9 patients (78%) reporting >50% improvement in sleep inertia and brain fog. Adverse effects included worsening depression, mild appetite suppression, and insomnia from improper capsule administration, which resolved with counseling. One patient's refractory symptoms were attributed to undiagnosed obstructive sleep apnea, which responded to continuous positive airway pressure. Nightly delayed-release methylphenidate was associated with meaningful improvement in early morning sleep inertia and brain fog severity in the majority of this small pediatric cohort with symptoms refractory to standard therapy. Larger, controlled studies are needed to establish efficacy, optimal dosing, and patient selection criteria.

papers.title: Sleep quality, atrial fibrillation burden, and symptom severity in patients with atrial fibrillation: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and may be associated with greater AF burden and more severe AF-related symptoms. However, evidence linking sleep quality to AF-related patient-reported outcomes remains limited. To evaluate sleep quality, AF burden, AF-related symptom severity, and global well-being in patients with AF and to examine the associations between sleep quality and these outcomes. This descriptive cross-sectional study included 122 patients with AF attending the cardiology outpatient clinic of a public hospital. Data were collected using a patient information form, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the University of Toronto Atrial Fibrillation Severity Scale (AFSS). Analyses included independent-samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation, and multivariable linear regression. The mean PSQI score was 7.60 ± 3.29, and 77% of participants were classified as having poor sleep quality. Mean AFSS Global Well-being, AF Burden, and Symptom scores were 4.96 ± 1.93, 13.98 ± 5.40, and 9.42 ± 5.14, respectively. After adjustment for age, sex, BMI, AF duration, additional cardiac disease, and alcohol use, higher PSQI scores were associated with lower Global Well-being (β = -0.231, p = 0.013), higher AF Burden (β = 0.444, p < 0.001), and greater symptom severity (β = 0.453, p < 0.001). Poorer sleep quality was associated with lower global well-being, greater AF burden, and more severe AF-related symptoms. These findings support routine sleep assessment and individualized care in patients with AF.
papers.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

papers.title: Light pollution causes death, sleep loss, and cognitive impairments through systemic reactive oxygen species accumulation in bumblebee (Bombus terrestris) gynes.
papers.abstract: Light pollution affects about one quarter of the Earth's land surface and is rapidly growing in both extent and intensity with accelerated global urbanization. Artificial light at night (ALAN) constitutes the major source of light pollution and poses significant challenges to the health of many organisms, including pollinators. However, whether and how ALAN exposure affects bumblebees' physiology remain unexplored. Our study aims to preliminarily investigate the effects of ALAN exposure on bumblebees and hypothesizes that it may cause physiological damage to gynes. As we expected, ALAN exposure causes precocious death in gynes. Extended light exposure leads to sleep loss and dysfunctional cognitive performance in gynes. In addition, light pollution also disrupts the nutritional homeostasis in gynes. Transcriptomic analysis revealed altered expression of genes associated with sleep, cognition, and nutrient metabolism, suggesting that ALAN exposure may disrupt gut-brain communication in gynes. Furthermore, systemic accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) is detected in ALAN-exposed gynes due to down-regulation of genes in the glutathione metabolic pathway. Importantly, both oral supplementation with antioxidants and dark recovery effectively suppress excessive ROS production and reverse the detrimental effects after ALAN exposure to gynes. Our study provides evidence of the detrimental effects of light pollution on gynes for the first time and reveals the pivotal role of oxidative stress in mediating light-induced sleep loss, cognitive impairment, and nutrient homeostasis disruption of bumblebees. This further implicates light pollution as a potential contributor to bumblebees' decline.

papers.title: Optically-pumped magnetometer-MEG (OPM-MEG) can detect and map epileptiform activity in diagnostic and presurgical paediatric cohorts.
papers.abstract: Several studies have now demonstrated that OPM-MEG can be used to detect interictal epileptiform activity in both adults and children. The potential reduced costs and increased tolerability afforded by OPM-MEG could increase the clinical utility of the technique to encompass patients who are at the diagnostic stage. We aimed to demonstrate use in both diagnostic and presurgical patients, with high concordance relative to clinical profiles and previous clinical EEGs. We were particularly interested in demonstrating use in a wider presentation of epilepsy, particularly in those with autism and associated comorbid conditions who generally find EEG more difficult to tolerate. 17 paediatric patients were recorded (7 presurgical; 10 diagnostic). Number of detected epileptiform events, recording length, and patient feedback were used as measures of diagnostic yield and tolerability. Equivalent current dipole mapping was used to localise epileptiform activity (e.g. spikes/sharp waves) and results were compared with clinical history for concordance. OPM-MEG recordings were tolerated well. The average number of detected epileptiform events for the presurgical cohort was 35 with a SD of 33 instances per participant, and for the diagnostic cohort was 39 with a SD of 78 instances per participant. One presurgical cohort participant and four diagnostic cohort participants did not show any epileptiform activity during the recording time. This study demonstrates that OPM-MEG can be used to detect interictal epileptiform activity in a diverse cohort of paediatric patients, in both focal and generalised epilepsies. This work provides evidence for a use-case earlier in the evaluation of paediatric epilepsy.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: Predicting the risk of seizure recurrence after antiseizure medication withdrawal in children with epilepsy: An individualized and web-based clinical decision support model.
papers.abstract: To determine seizure recurrence rates and independent risk factors following antiseizure medication (ASM) withdrawal in pediatric epilepsy, and integrate these findings into a personalized web-based clinical decision support system (CDSS). In this prospective cohort study, 318 pediatric epilepsy patients with ≥24 months of clinical seizure freedom and completely normal pre-withdrawal EEGs were evaluated during ASM withdrawal. Independent risk factors were identified using a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model and embedded into a dynamic web tool. Seizure recurrence occurred in 25.8% (n = 82) of patients (mean time: 4.70 ± 13.96 months). The Cox model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (C-index = 0.808, optimism-corrected C-index = 0.769). Independent predictors of recurrence were status epilepticus (SE; HR = 2.718, 95% CI: 1.193-6.194; p = 0.017), febrile seizures (FS; HR = 2.300, 95% CI: 1.214-4.356; p = 0.011), and active epilepsy duration (HR = 1.022 per month, 95% CI: 1.016-1.027; p < 0.001). Compared to ≤24 months, pre-withdrawal seizure freedom of 25-35 months (HR = 0.231, p = 0.001) and ≥36 months (HR = 0.232, p = 0.002) both conferred an approximate 77% risk reduction. Mandatory pre-withdrawal EEG normalization served as a controlled methodological feature isolating clinical predictors in EEG-normal children. Among 35 patients undergoing a second withdrawal attempt, 11 (31.4%) experienced recurrence. SE, FS, active epilepsy duration, and pre-withdrawal seizure-free duration independently predict recurrence in children with normal pre-withdrawal EEGs. Embedding this model into a web tool enables dynamic, evidence-based risk stratification in pediatric practice.

papers.title: The prevalence and risk factors of night eating syndrome among university students: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: To estimate the pooled proportion of night eating syndrome (NES) outcomes among university students and identify associated factors through a systematic review and meta-analysis. We searched the China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Database, Weipu Database, Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar to identify studies reporting NES outcomes and associated factors among university students. Backward citation searching was also conducted to identify additional eligible studies. We performed meta-analyses to estimate the pooled proportion of NES outcomes and identify associated factors. Forty-two studies involving university students from 16 countries were included. The pooled proportion of NES outcomes was 19% (95% CI: 0.13-0.25), with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 99.85%). Subgroup analysis showed statistically significant differences in pooled proportions across assessment methods (P = 0.004). Male sex (OR = 2.11, 95% CI: 1.57-2.83), smoking (OR = 2.46, 95% CI: 1.74-3.47), depression (OR = 5.03, 95% CI: 1.48-17.17), stress (OR = 3.05, 95% CI: 1.60-5.84), and poor sleep quality or insomnia (OR = 3.38, 95% CI: 1.93-5.92) were significantly associated with NES outcomes. The pooled proportion of NES outcomes among university students was 19%. Male sex, smoking, depression, stress, and poor sleep quality or insomnia were significantly associated with NES outcomes. These findings should be interpreted in the context of the substantial heterogeneity across studies.

papers.title: Sports-Related Concussion in Adolescents: Epidemiology, Assessment, Management, and Return to Sport.
papers.abstract: The accurate diagnosis and appropriate management of sports-related concussions in children and adolescents are high priorities for healthcare providers. Sports-related concussion remains a clinical diagnosis. In the acute setting, sideline tools such as the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 5/Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 6 are most valuable, and in the clinical setting, these assessment tools can serve as adjuncts to a comprehensive history and physical examination, including vestibular ocular motor screening. Management includes brief relative rest followed by an individualized approach for return to school and sport that is largely dependent on symptoms. Recovery also should be supported by good sleep, hydration, and nutrition. For patients with prolonged symptoms persisting beyond 30 days, a multidisciplinary, targeted approach to address underlying factors contributes to prolonged recovery.

papers.title: AIM-STAGE: a self-supervised framework via adaptive interval-aware multi-kernel calibration and spectro-temporal exploration for few-shot EEG staging.
papers.abstract: Learning discriminative and generalizable representations fromelectroencephalography (EEG) signals with limited annotations remains a key challenge inautomatic sleep staging. Supervised deep models depend on large-scale expert labels, yetsleep annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing self-supervised methods oftenunderuse EEG spectral-temporal structure and adopt fixed negative-sample strategies,which are poorly suited to the continuous transitions and ambiguous boundaries betweensleep stages. This study proposes AIM-STAGE, a self-supervised representation learningframework for limited-label EEG sleep staging. AIM-STAGE comprises threemodules. (1) Spectral-temporal exploration: maps EEG segments into the time-frequencydomain through the short-time Fourier transform (STFT), jointly extracting log-powerand cross-channel phase difference to characterize frequency-band activity and phasedynamics. (2) Local-global hybrid encoding: uses a CNN-Transformer encoder, in whichconvolutional residual modules capture local spectro-temporal patterns and a bottleneckTransformer models long-range dependencies. (3) Adaptive interval-aware multi-kernelcalibration: employs multiple Gaussian kernels and dynamic weighting to synthesizeinformative negative representations, improving view consistency and inter-sampleseparability. AIM-STAGE was evaluated on SLEEP-2013, SLEEP-2018,SHHS-D, and SHHS-H against ContraWR, DFformer, EEG2Rep, EEGPT, Superlet-MAE,and a supervised baseline across 1% to 15% labels. Accuracy improved from 88.67% to92.04% on SLEEP-2013, and AIM-STAGE outperformed all baselines on all four datasetswith higher kappa, macro-F1, and balanced accuracy, including on the pathologicalSHHS-D cohort. Ablation confirmed the contributions of the bottleneck Transformer,positional embeddings, physiology-informed augmentation, and calibration loss. Per-stageanalysis showed that N1 is the most difficult stage, with F1 ranging from 0.003 to 0.046,and adding EOG and EMG markedly improved its precision, recall, and F1. AIM-STAGE offers an interpretable and label-efficient self-supervised solution for EEGsleep staging, improving robustness and stage discriminability under scarce-labelconditions while reducing dependence on manual annotation.&#xD.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of biosignal foundation models.
papers.abstract: Foundation models are emerging as a promising approach to biosignal analysis, offering solutions to common challenges in learning from biosignal data, such as high variability, noise or limited annotations. This survey provides a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art in this rapidly advancing field. We introduce commonly used biosignal modalities (including EEG, ECG, EMG, EOG and PPG) and discuss their defining characteristics with respect to training large models. We present a structured survey of existing work across unimodal and multimodal settings covering data processing, feature extraction, model architectures, pre-training paradigms and evaluation methods. We identify open challenges such as benchmarking, interpretability and data availability and highlight possible directions for future research. By consolidating our findings from the current literature and opportunities for progress, we aim to guide the development of robust and universal foundation models for biosignals.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates TNBS-induced visceral pain and modulates cortical EEG rhythms in association with TREM1/DAP12 pathway inhibition: Enhanced effects with pharmacological TREM1 blockade.
papers.abstract: BackgroundVisceral pain in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) lacks effective therapies. Whether the TREM1/DAP12 pathway is associated with electroacupuncture (EA) analgesia and cortical EEG modulation remains unclear.ObjectiveTo determine if spinal TREM1/DAP12 is associated with EA's analgesic and neuromodulatory effects in TNBS-induced visceral pain.MethodsMale Sprague-Dawley rats with TNBS-induced colitis received EA (ST36/ST37), the TREM1 inhibitor Nangibotide, or their combination. Behaviors (PWT, CRD, DAI), spinal TREM1/DAP12, downstream inflammatory mediators, and microglial colocalization were evaluated. Cortical EEG was analyzed using normalized power spectral density (Normalized PSD, %).ResultsEA significantly alleviated visceral/referred hyperalgesia and reduced DAI scores (P < 0.05). TNBS upregulated spinal TREM1, DAP12, TNF-α, NLRP3, and TLR4 and increased TREM1/DAP12 microglial colocalization (P < 0.0001), all reversed by EA (P < 0.001). Nangibotide alone partially mimicked EA's effects, and their combination yielded greater analgesia and molecular suppression (P < 0.05). Normalized EEG analysis revealed that TNBS increased δ power (P < 0.0001) and reduced θ and β power (P < 0.001). Notably, EA and Nangibotide specifically reversed δ elevation and restored θ power (P<0.05) without altering β power (P > 0.05), with greater δ suppression than either treatment alone (P < 0.0001).ConclusionEA alleviates TNBS visceral pain and normalizes cortical δ/θ dysrhythmia, with these effects associated with suppression of microglial TREM1/DAP12 neuroinflammation. Pharmacological TREM1 blockade mimics and enhances EA's effects, supporting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for visceral pain.

papers.title: Supporting the driver's perception cognition action loop using an embodied intelligent cockpit framework for explainable fatigue intervention.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated a driver-support framework combining multimodal fatigue detection, feature attribution, and state-specific auditory feedback during conditional automated driving. Forty licensed drivers completed three counterbalanced 20-min simulator conditions: nonverbal warnings, generic speech, and explanatory speech. A fixed detector used electroencephalography (EEG), eye tracking, and vehicle dynamics. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) selected a dominant cue, which a large language model translated into a spoken message. Fatigue labels were based on the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale and a 60-s vigilance task. Braking reaction time, standard deviation of lane position (SDLP), and time-to-collision (TTC) exposure were assessed during manual driving following takeover. Compared with generic speech, explanatory speech was associated with a 0.192-s shorter mean braking reaction time (95% confidence interval: -0.223 to -0.161 s; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and a 0.085-m lower mean SDLP (95% confidence interval: -0.108 to -0.062 m; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). The mean proportion of time with TTC < 1.5 s was 0.07 versus 0.10. Retrospective leave-one-subject-out evaluation yielded an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.85. The explanatory warning package was associated with faster braking and more stable lane keeping than generic speech in this simulator study. Further studies should separate message content from acoustic properties and assess performance in independent driving settings.

papers.title: Dietary Vitamin K2 Intake, Musculoskeletal Injury, and Cardiometabolic Health in Service Members.
papers.abstract: Vitamin K2 (K2) research has demonstrated that with sufficient K2 intake, vitamin K-dependent proteins are activated to regulate bone diseases and inflammation-related diseases, offering an innovative strategy to address ongoing musculoskeletal injury (MSKi) and high adiposity challenges that threaten health promotion, performance, and readiness in service members (SMs). This study aimed to characterize K2 status in a military sample and explore the relationship between dietary K2 intake and bone health, metabolic health, and inflammation status in the context of SM health and operational readiness or deployability. At baseline and 12 months, Army and Air Force units provided data from demographic and food frequency questionnaires, body composition, bone density, cardiometabolic, and biomarker measurements. Activity trackers monitored physical activity and sleep duration continuously. Between August 2023 and July 2024, we enrolled 47 active duty SMs. The sample was predominantly male, racially and ethnically diverse, averaged 27 years of age, and had an average of 6.5 years of service. At baseline, 45% met the criteria for stage I hypertension and 45% exceeded military body fat standards. Participants reported insufficient baseline dietary intake of vitamin K1+K2 and vitamin D. Over the 12 months, fermented food consumption slightly increased, activity behaviors remained unchanged, and participants self-reported 10 noncombat MSKis. Participants reported no significant changes in body composition, body fat specifically, or dietary intake of vitamin D or vitamin K2. Exploratory proteomics analysis identified links between K2 and inflammation, bone architecture, glucose homeostasis, and insulin receptors. MSKi, high body fat, and meeting optimal nutrition goals remain readiness challenges for SMs. Exploring K2 identified meaningful metrics and actionable strategies to address these challenges. Highlighting data-informed interventions adds to nursing's nutritional and cardiometabolic knowledge base and clinical interventions, as the nursing workforce is positioned to influence every step of patient care: conducting research, generating data to inform clinical practice and interventions, and ensuring evidence-based patient education and counseling to optimize SM health and readiness.

papers.title: CsLUX-CsPME6/CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 modulates pectin methylesterification to coordinate cold tolerance and growth in tea plants.
papers.abstract: Cell wall pectin methylesterification is critical for plant defense and development, yet how it coordinately regulates cold tolerance and growth in perennial crops remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that cold stress significantly reduces the degree of methylesterification (DM) of pectin in tea plants, concurrent with extensive remodeling of cellular and subcellular structures, including enhanced xylem development, altered mesophyll architecture, and impaired chloroplast morphology. Genome-wide analysis identifies 100 pectin methylesterase (PME) and 42 PME inhibitor (PMEI) genes, among which CsPME6, CsPMEI8, and CsPMEI17 exhibit cold-responsive expression and localize to the nucleus and apoplast. Functional studies demonstrate that CsPME6 positively regulates cold tolerance in tea plants, while CsPMEI8 and CsPMEI17 act as negative regulators. Mechanistically, CsPME6 elevates PME activity to lower pectin DM, whereas CsPMEI8 directly inhibit CsPME6 activity to maintain high pectin DM. Also, CsPMEI17 also negatively enhanced total PME activity to enhance the cold tolerance in tea plants. Notably, our findings suggested that the circadian clock component CsLUX directly binds to the LBS motifs in the promoters of these three genes, activating CsPME6 and repressing CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 expression, which contributes to pectin methylesterification homeostasis. Besides, CsLUX-CsPME6/CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 module also promote glutamate/γ-aminobutyric acid metabolism, leaf thickness, plant height, and root elongation in tea plants. Our findings underscore the importance of pectin methylesterification dynamics mediated by CsLUX-CsPME/PMEI involving cold tolerance and growth development in tea plants.

papers.title: Understanding the Link Between Eveningness and Depression: A Serial Mediation Study of Daytime Sleepiness and Pre-Sleep Arousal.
papers.abstract: The evening chronotype is consistently associated with depressive symptoms, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study examined whether daytime sleepiness and pre-sleep arousal mediate the relationship between eveningness and depressive symptoms in adults. In this cross-sectional study, 524 adults were recruited from community health centers in Indonesia using convenience sampling. Chronotype, daytime sleepiness, pre-sleep arousal, and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Pre-Sleep Arousal Scale (PSAS), and Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS), respectively. Serial mediation analysis adjusted for age and gender was performed, with indirect effects tested using 5000 bootstrap resamples; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for caffeine consumption and sleep medication use. Participants with depressive symptoms had lower MEQ scores and higher ESS and PSAS scores than those without (all p < 0.001). Eveningness was associated with greater depressive symptoms both directly and indirectly through daytime sleepiness and pre-sleep arousal. Eveningness retained a significant direct effect (69% of the total effect), indicating partial mediation. Pre-sleep arousal showed the strongest indirect effect (21.1% of the total effect), followed by the serial pathway through daytime sleepiness and pre-sleep arousal (5.6%) and daytime sleepiness alone (4.3%). Results were similar after additional adjustment. Daytime sleepiness and pre-sleep arousal partially mediated the relationship between eveningness and depressive symptoms, with pre-sleep arousal emerging as the strongest pathway. Interventions targeting bedtime hyperarousal may help reduce depressive symptoms in evening-type individuals, alongside approaches addressing other contributing mechanisms.

papers.title: Effect of Acoustic Environment Improvement Combined with Roy Adaptation Model-Based Supportive Nursing on Self-Efficacy and Maternal Role Adaptation in Advanced-Age Primiparas.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effect of acoustic environment improvement combined with Roy adaptation model (RAM)-based supportive nursing on self-efficacy and maternal role adaptation in advanced-age primiparas. This retrospective cohort study included 158 eligible advanced-age primiparas who gave birth in the obstetrics department of the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University between February 2025 and February 2026. The primiparas were divided into a control group ( n = 80) and an observation group ( n = 78) according to the nursing method they actually received. The control group received RAM-based supportive nursing care, whereas the observation group received acoustic environment improvement combined with RAM-based supportive nursing care. The Perceived Maternal Parenting Self-Efficacy scale, Maternal Role Adaptation Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), time to first lactation, and exclusive breastfeeding rate were compared between the two groups before and after nursing. Repeated-measures analysis of variance showed significant effects of time, group, and time × group interaction on maternal role adaptation scores (all P < 0.05). Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons demonstrated significant within-group changes over time (all adjusted P < 0.05), and the observation group had higher scores than the control group at discharge and 6 weeks postpartum (both P < 0.05). For PSQI scores, significant effects of time ( P < 0.001), group ( P = 0.003), and time × group interaction ( P = 0.039) were observed. The observation group showed lower PSQI scores than the control group at discharge and 6 weeks postpartum ( P = 0.004 and P = 0.001, respectively). Time to first lactation in the observation group was significantly shorter than that in the control group (24.87 ± 3.53 h vs. 28.21 ± 4.12 h; P < 0.001). At 6 weeks postpartum, the exclusive breastfeeding rate was significantly higher in the observation group than in the control group (76.9% vs. 62.5%; P = 0.049). Among advanced-age primiparas, acoustic environment improvement combined with RAM-based supportive nursing was associated with improved sleep quality, enhanced self-efficacy and neonatal care capabilities, and promoted maternal role adaptation, and may help promote lactation and increase the exclusive breastfeeding rate.

papers.title: Effects of Noise Reduction Management on Anxiety, Sleep Quality, and Early Postoperative Stress Responses in Patients After Thoracoscopic Lung Surgery.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of systematic noise reduction management on postoperative anxiety, sleep quality, and early stress responses in patients undergoing elective thoracoscopic lung surgery. This retrospective cohort study enrolled 150 patients who underwent elective thoracoscopic lung surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University in 2025. Patients were divided into a control group ( n = 75) receiving routine nursing care and an observation group ( n = 75) additionally receiving systematic noise reduction management. Anxiety (Self-Rating Anxiety Scale, SAS), sleep quality (Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire, RCSQ), heart rate variability (HRV) indices (standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals [SDNN], root mean square of successive differences [RMSSD], and low-frequency/high-frequency ratio [LF/HF]), and stress markers (serum cortisol [Cor], C-reactive protein [CRP], and procalcitonin [PCT]) were compared between groups at 1 day before surgery and at 1 and 6 days after surgery. Daytime, nighttime, and 24-hour noise levels were significantly lower in the observation group than in the control group (all P < 0.01). At 1 day after surgery, SAS scores increased and RCSQ scores decreased in both groups, with no significant intergroup differences ( P > 0.05). At 6 days after surgery, the observation group had significantly lower SAS scores (52.67 ± 5.21 versus 55.33 ± 6.85, P = 0.008) and higher RCSQ scores (48.45 ± 6.54 versus 40.87 ± 5.92, P < 0.001). Serum Cor, CRP, and PCT increased in both groups at day 1 and decreased by day 6, when they were significantly lower in the observation group (Cor 380.80 ± 42.79 versus 402.45 ± 32.43 nmol/L, P < 0.001; CRP 39.56 ± 6.33 versus 48.34 ± 7.89 mg/L, P < 0.001; PCT 0.12 ± 0.06 versus 0.15 ± 0.08 ng/mL, P = 0.017). HRV indices decreased at day 1 and recovered by day 6, when SDNN, RMSSD, and LF/HF were significantly higher in the observation group (all P < 0.01). Systematic noise reduction management was associated with lower anxiety levels, improved sleep quality, and attenuated early postoperative stress responses after thoracoscopic lung surgery, supporting its value as an adjunct to routine nursing care.

papers.title: Occupational Health Outcomes Among Staff Working in Low-, Medium-, and High-Noise Zones of the Central Sterile Supply Department and Operating Room.
papers.abstract: To explore the associations between noise exposure and occupational health indicators among staff working in the central sterile supply department (CSSD) and operating room. This cross-sectional observational study included 100 healthcare technicians working in the CSSD and operating room between January 2025 and February 2026. Based on the noise monitoring data of the hospital, the work zones were categorized into low-noise zone (<65 dB), medium-noise zone (65-75 dB), and high-noise zone (>75 dB) according to the equivalent continuous sound levels. Outcomes included hearing discomfort, tinnitus, sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [PSQI]), attentional performance (Digit Cancellation Test), mental fatigue (Mental Fatigue Scale), perceived workload (the NASA Task Load Index [NASA-TLX]), and thermal discomfort. A binary logistic regression model was used to analyze the association between noise exposure levels and occupational health outcomes. Compared with staff working in the low-noise zone, those working in high-noise zones had a higher incidence of hearing discomfort and tinnitus ( P < 0.05), and higher PSQI scores ( P < 0.01). High-noise exposure was significantly associated with poorer attentional performance and greater mental fatigue ( P < 0.01). The NASA-TLX total score in the high-noise zone was significantly higher than that in the low-noise zone ( P < 0.01), with the greatest differences observed in mental demand and temporal demand dimensions. In binary logistic regression analysis, staff working in high-noise zones had higher odds of tinnitus (OR = 3.82, 95% CI: 1.92-7.61, P < 0.001) and hearing discomfort (OR = 4.25, 95% CI: 2.11-8.56, P < 0.001). Higher occupational noise exposure was associated with hearing discomfort, poorer sleep quality, greater mental fatigue, poorer attentional performance, and higher perceived workload among staff working in CSSDs and operating rooms.

papers.title: Latent Profile Analysis of Psychosocial Adjustment and Subjective Noise Annoyance in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy.
papers.abstract: To identify latent profiles of psychosocial adjustment and subjective noise annoyance in patients with diabetic retinopathy (DR) and to analyze disease-related factors. This cross-sectional survey included 198 patients with DR. Participants completed the Psychosocial Adjustment to Illness Scale-Self Report (PAIS-SR), a subjective noise annoyance rating, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), and the Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). Latent profile analysis was performed using the PAIS-SR domain scores and subjective noise annoyance scores as indicators. Multinomial logistic regression was used to identify demographic and disease-related factors associated with profile membership. Three profiles were identified: a well-adjusted profile (35.4%), an intermediate-adjustment profile (41.9%), and a high-annoyance/poor-adjustment profile (22.7%), with an entropy of 0.922. Patients in the high-annoyance/poor-adjustment profile had poorer sleep quality, higher anxiety levels, and lower social support than those in the other profiles, with significant differences in PSQI, SAS, and SSRS scores across the three profiles (all P < 0.001). Multinomial logistic regression showed that longer diabetes duration, proliferative DR, and poorer worse-eye best-corrected visual acuity were associated with membership in the less favorable profiles. For the high-annoyance/poor-adjustment profile, the corresponding odds ratios (ORs) were 1.138, 3.599, and 1.259, respectively. Diabetic macular edema showed a borderline association with this profile (OR = 2.455, P = 0.050). Psychosocial adjustment and noise annoyance patterns are heterogeneous among patients with DR. Identifying patients with a high-annoyance/poor-adjustment profile may support noise management and stratified nursing care.

papers.title: Effects of Noise Reduction Combined with AI-Based Nursing System on Postoperative Sleep Quality and Delirium Incidence in Older Patients with Severe Glioma.
papers.abstract: To explore the effect of noise reduction combined with the artificial intelligence (AI)-based nursing system on postoperative care in older patients with severe glioma. This retrospective analysis included 100 older patients with severe glioma admitted to Zhoukou Orthopedic Hospital between October 2020 and December 2025. Patients were assigned to the combined nursing group and the control group according to different nursing methods. Sleep quality, the incidence and duration of delirium, the incidence of postoperative complications, and nursing satisfaction were compared between the two groups at 7 and 14 days after surgery. At 7 and 14 days after surgery, the total and each dimension score of the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire in the combined nursing group were significantly higher than those in the control group ( P < 0.05). The combined nursing group had a lower incidence of delirium (7.27% versus 26.67%) and a shorter duration of delirium than the control group (both P < 0.05). The combined nursing group also had a lower incidence of postoperative complications (5.45% versus 22.22%) and a higher nursing satisfaction rate (96.36% versus 77.78%) than the control group (both P < 0.05). After adjustment for potential confounders, noise reduction combined with the AI-based nursing system was associated with significantly lower odds of postoperative delirium compared with routine care alone (OR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.06-0.78, P = 0.019). The combined intervention of noise reduction and AI-based nursing system was associated with a more favorable postoperative prognosis among older patients with severe glioma. It may help optimize postoperative nursing strategies for this patient population, although further verification is warranted.

papers.title: Effects of Noise Exposure on Sleep Quality and Dyspnea Perception in Hospitalized Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: To prospectively investigate the effects of noise exposure on sleep quality and dyspnea perception in hospitalized chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patients. 128 COPD inpatients (January 2024 to December 2025) at the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University were enrolled. A portable sound level meter continuously monitored noise intensity for 72 h. Patients were divided into low (≤45 dB, n = 37), medium (46-60 dB, n = 65), and high (>60 dB, n = 26) noise exposure groups. Sleep quality was assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), dyspnea by the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) scale and Borg scale. The high exposure group had significantly higher PSQI total scores (18.71 ± 3.82 versus 13.75 ± 3.36 versus 6.36 ± 0.84, P < 0.001), higher proportion of mMRC scores of 3-4, and higher Borg scores (rest: 4.38 ± 1.03 versus 3.26 ± 0.92 versus 2.17 ± 0.84; post-activity: 7.12 ± 1.34 versus 5.74 ± 1.26 versus 4.29 ± 1.13, all P < 0.05). Noise intensity positively correlated with PSQI score ( r = 0.782, P < 0.001) and Borg score ( r = 0.683, P < 0.001). Multivariate linear regression analysis further demonstrated that noise exposure intensity (per 10 dB increment) was independently associated with both PSQI total score ( B = 2.45, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.98-2.92, β = 0.68, P < 0.001) and post-activity Borg score ( B = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.08-1.96, β = 0.58, P < 0.001), after adjusting for age, Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease grade, disease duration, and hypnotic drug use. Higher noise exposure is associated with poorer sleep quality and more pronounced dyspnea perception in hospitalized COPD patients. Effective noise control measures should be implemented.

papers.title: Effects of Plan-Do-Check-Act Cycle Nursing Combined with Noise Management on Sleep and Clinical Outcomes in Children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia Complicated by Encephalitis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effects of Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle nursing combined with noise management on sleep indicators and clinical outcomes during hospitalization among children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) complicated by encephalitis. A retrospective analysis was conducted. A total of 100 children were classified into an observation group and a control group according to the nursing care actually received during hospitalization, with 50 children in each group. The control group received routine nursing care, whereas the observation group received PDCA cycle nursing combined with noise management in addition to routine nursing care. Baseline characteristics, sleep quality indicators, clinical improvement outcomes, biomarker indices, and the incidence of complications were compared between the two groups. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable between the two groups. After nursing care, the observation group had longer total sleep duration [8.0 (7.0, 8.5) h versus 7.5 (7.0, 8.0) h, P = 0.019], fewer awakenings [2.0 (1.0, 3.0) versus 3.0 (2.0, 4.0), P = 0.005], and fewer crying/startle episodes [1.0 (0.0, 2.0) versus 2.0 (1.0, 3.0), P = 0.009]. Fever duration and time to cough relief were also shorter in the observation group ( P = 0.004 and P = 0.010). Several inflammatory, neurological injury-related, and cerebrospinal fluid indicators differed significantly after nursing care. The overall complication rate was lower in the observation group (26.00% versus 48.00%, P = 0.023). Compared with routine nursing alone, the addition of PDCA cycle nursing combined with noise management was associated with greater improvement in sleep during hospitalization, faster relief of clinical symptoms, and a lower overall incidence of complications in children with MPP complicated by encephalitis, suggesting its potential value in optimizing nursing management for this population.

papers.title: Effects of Personalized Noise Reduction Combined with Comfort Care on Pain and Negative Emotions in Patients with Acute Pancreatitis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of personalized noise reduction combined with comfort care on pain, negative emotions, and sleep quality in patients with acute pancreatitis (AP) who are hospitalized. This retrospective study included 80 AP patients admitted between January 2022 and July 2025. The patients were divided into a comfort care group ( n = 39) receiving routine nursing care plus standardized comfort care, and a combined care group ( n = 41) additionally receiving personalized noise reduction management. The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain, the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), the Single-Item Sleep Quality Scale (SQS), the EuroQol Five-Dimension Five-Level (EQ-5D-5L), and the Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire-18(PSQ-18) scores were compared before and after 7 days of care. Continuous variables were analyzed using independent samples t-test for between-group comparisons and paired t-test for within-group comparisons. Categorical variables were compared using the chi-squared test. P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Before care implementation, VAS, SAS, SDS, SQS, and EQ-5D-5L scores showed no statistically significant differences between the two groups ( P > 0.05). After 7 days of care, VAS, SAS, and SDS scores in both groups were significantly lower than before care ( P < 0.05). After care, the combined care group showed significantly lower scores than the comfort care group ( P < 0.05). SQS and EQ-5D-5L scores in both groups were significantly higher than before care ( P < 0.05). After care, the combined care group showed significantly higher scores than the comfort care group ( P < 0.05). PSQ-18 scores on day 7 showed significantly higher patient satisfaction in the combined care group than in the comfort care group ( P < 0.05). Personalized noise reduction combined with comfort care is a more effective way of alleviating pain, negative emotions, and sleep disturbances in AP patients than comfort care alone. This approach enriches comprehensive nursing with individualized acoustic environment management. However, due to the retrospective design of this study, prospective randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Nonauditory Effects of Infrasound and Low-Frequency Noise in Humans: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: This systematic review aimed to assess the quality of evidence across studies on the nonauditory effects of infrasound (IS) and low-frequency noise (LFN) in adults, investigating physiological and psychological outcomes associated with such exposures. Studies were searched in eight databases from their earliest records up to March 2026. Outcomes assessed included annoyance and noise sensitivity, sleep disturbances, cardiovascular diseases, cognitive and mental health impairments, and other health-related disturbances. The quality of evidence for each outcome was assessed using an adapted Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. The review included 39 papers, predominantly cross-sectional designs (laboratory-based and real-life), with fewer cohort studies and only three randomized controlled trials. Exposure scenarios varied widely, encompassing wind turbine noise, traffic and community noise, occupational noise, and experimentally generated IS and/or LFN stimuli. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate for annoyance/sensitivity to very low for sleep disturbance, cardiovascular outcomes, cognitive performance, mental health, and general health disturbances. These ratings were influenced by the predominance of cross-sectional studies, high overall risk of bias, methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent findings, and indirectness across outcomes. The findings showed that annoyance and sensitivity were the only outcomes associated with exposure to IS/LFN, supported by moderate-quality evidence, suggesting that these subjective responses should be included in health impact assessments. For all other outcomes, the certainty of the evidence remains very low, highlighting the urgent need for well-designed longitudinal and experimental studies.

papers.title: Noise Pollution in Cement Manufacturing Industries: A Comprehensive Review of Environmental and Occupational Health Impacts and Mitigation Strategies.
papers.abstract: The process of cement production is a somewhat neglected yet considerable contributor to noise pollution both in the workplace and its surroundings, as it produces high-intensity noise through various activities such as crushing, grinding, and heating. In the paper that follows, recent literature concerning the sources and effects of noise pollution in cement production is analyzed, and the effectiveness of various noise mitigation strategies is assessed. Publications from 2015 to 2025 were reviewed, along with some prior publications, focusing on various noise sources, effects on workers and the environment, and noise mitigation strategies. Loudness in cement-producing plants is about 68.8-103.3 dB(A) and is continuous in nature, unlike other industries' processes, which are characterized by sound bursts only. Subsequent effects on job-related experiences and workers' functioning include negative effects on hearing ability, heart problems, sleep disorders, and stress, which increases considerably due to the mixture of loudness with dust and chemicals; noise impacts animals' behavior, communication, and habitat. Together, engineering controls, administrative controls, and spatial planning in facilities form a structured control hierarchy that has proven to be effective. However, its implementation is hampered by high cost and inconsistent regulation across regions of the world. Most of the evidence for the reliability of this approach comes from cross-sectional studies of single factories with scarce longitudinal data. Hence, noise pollution in the cement production process presents a major multi-faceted risk for employees, and to mitigate this risk effectively, coordinated engineering, administrative, and regulatory measures must be applied.

papers.title: Protocol for cell-type-specific circadian bioluminescence recording from mouse gut muscularis externa explants.
papers.abstract: Cell-type-specific circadian recording is essential for understanding tissue-level circadian organization. This protocol describes the generation of intestinal cell-type-specific PER2::CBG-LUC reporter mice, preparation of intestinal longitudinal muscle-myenteric plexus explants, long-term bioluminescence recording using photomultiplier-based photon counting system, and analysis of circadian phase and rhythmicity. The protocol also includes procedures to verify that ex vivo rhythms reflect the endogenous in vivo circadian phase. For complete details on the execution of this protocol, please refer to Magaña et al.1.

papers.title: Targeted gene therapy alleviates epilepsy and hyperexcitability in models of SCN2A deficiency.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic SCN2A loss-of-function (LoF) variants can cause severe, refractory epilepsy with limited treatment options. Existing Scn2a-LoF mouse models exhibit few spontaneous seizures, limiting the dynamic range needed to assess therapeutic efficacy. We therefore generated gene-trap Scn2a-deficient mice on the seizure-prone DBA/2J background. These mice experienced hundreds of spontaneous absence seizures per day, characterized by concurrent behavioral arrest and EEG spike-wave discharges (SWDs). Partial restoration of Scn2a expression reduced seizure burden. Electrophysiological analysis revealed impaired action potential waveforms yet increased repetitive firing, alongside coordinated downregulation of voltage-gated potassium channel genes, potentially contributing to hyperexcitability. Given the broad potassium channel downregulation and prior efficacy of KCNA1 gene therapy in refractory seizure models, we selected KV1.1 as a potential therapeutic target and used a drug-controllable adeno-associated virus (AAV) to express human KCNA1. We found that this intervention normalized elevated neuronal firing and reduced spontaneous seizure burden in Scn2a-deficient mice. Extending these findings to a human cell-based platform, AAV-mediated KCNA1 expression also reduced neuronal firing in human cortical organoids carrying a SCN2A-truncating variant identified in patients. Together, these findings provide proof of principle for drug-controllable KCNA1 gene therapy as a promising treatment avenue for epilepsy related to SCN2A LoF variants.

papers.title: Late electroencephalographic seizure-risk findings and restricted diffusion on magnetic resonance imaging as seizure-burden markers associated with neurological deficits after status epilepticus in a remote or chronic cohort.
papers.abstract: To evaluate whether time-dependent electroencephalographic (EEG) seizure risk findings and restricted diffusion on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are associated with neurological outcomes after status epilepticus (SE), beyond seizure duration. This two-center observational study included consecutive SE patients from 2017 to 2025. We examined three seizure-related markers: seizure duration ≥ 30 min, a 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on a late EEG (performed the following day or later after SE onset), and SE-related restricted diffusion on MRI (peri-ictal diffusion-weighted imaging hyperintensity with reduced apparent diffusion coefficient values). Outcomes were overall neurological worsening and SE-attributable focal neurological deficits at discharge. Multivariable models included the three markers and age> 65 years, with further adjustment for stupor or coma at admission and third-line therapy. Of 440 patients with suspected SE, 297 had confirmed SE; 221 with an identified seizure focus formed the overall cohort; 127 with remote symptomatic SE or preexisting chronic focal epilepsy formed the remote or chronic cohort. Overall neurological worsening occurred in 96 patients (43.4%) and SE-attributable focal neurological deficits in 68 (30.8%). In univariable analyses, seizure duration ≥ 30 min was associated with both outcomes in the overall cohort. A 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on late EEG was associated with both outcomes in both cohorts, whereas high-risk findings on early EEG were not. In multivariable models including seizure duration, restricted diffusion was independently associated with both outcomes in both cohorts, most strongly with focal neurological deficits in the remote or chronic cohort (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 28.59, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 7.23-154.99). A 2HELPS2B score ≥ 2 on late EEG was independently associated with focal neurological deficits in the remote or chronic cohort (adjusted OR = 4.26, 95% CI = 1.35-14.24), whereas seizure duration ≥ 30 min was not independently associated with either outcome. High-risk late-EEG findings and restricted diffusion were associated with neurological deficits.
